The endpoint of Ladestien — Rotvollfjæra has a bathing dock, barbecue area and benches along the fjord, with train and bus within walking distance from Rotvoll station.
One of few bathing spots in Trondheim with restrooms, a barbecue and a bathing dock all in one place — Rotvoll train station is right nearby for an easy return after swimming.

Sjøtrappa is Trondheim's most democratic bathing spot — a simple descent along the harbour promenade where the fjord is right beneath you and the view towards Munkholmen makes you forget you're in the middle of a city.
The water is deep from the first step, which makes this spot as popular for winter swimming as it is for summer bathing — the cold-water society gathers here early in the morning year-round.

Skansenmoloen marks the western end of the harbour promenade where the Nidelva meets the fjord — a sheltered corner with a small grass area and beach volleyball courts, where everyday life by the water is well away from the tourist trails.
The mole provides good shelter from north-westerly winds, making this one of the calmest spots to sunbathe even when the rest of the quayside is breezy.

Strandveikaia in Nyhavna has lived many lives — from a white sandy beach locals called the Florida Coast, to the largest German U-boat harbour in Northern Europe during World War II, to today's year-round pilot bathing spot where the wartime quay buildings are listed as cultural monuments.
Water quality here is monitored twice a week throughout the year, making Strandveikaia one of Trondheim's most reliable spots for winter bathing in the city centre.

Close to the housing — suitable for children and dog owners.
Kaf is one of Bergen's busiest coffee spots at Bryggen — lively, warm and reliable.
Often full in tourist season but very accessible otherwise. Good bagels.
Indian restaurant by Bislett with a loyal neighbourhood following.
Known for consistently good food in a relaxed setting — a popular alternative to cooking at home.
Traditional Thai massage on the second floor of Sirkus Shopping — a quiet refuge amid the centre's bustle, offering everything from foot care to facials.
Book online and combine with shopping — perfect for a half-hour break that actually feels like a holiday.
KODE is Norway's largest art museum complex — the Stenersen building shows Norwegian and international modernism.
Rolling collection exhibitions. Combined tickets available for all KODE buildings.
Bar Circus has been Trondheim's rock bar for over 20 years — no cover charge, cheap beer, and good music on Olav Tryggvasons gate, where the regulars know each other by name.
Never a cover charge, always honest rock — opens at 8 PM Tuesday through Sunday.
Bergen Kunsthall is one of Norway's leading contemporary art centres — international exhibitions and local artists.
Programme rotates regularly. Good to combine with a Kode visit on Rasmus Meyers allé.
City park on Nordregata named after Stjørdal's pride — the Stjørdals-Blink sports club.
Green lung in the center — benches and playground for families with children.

Trondheim's grand hotel since 1870 — a Michelin star in Speilsalen, a wine bar with 10,000 bottles and afternoon tea in the Palmehaven.
Six distinct dining concepts under one historic roof — from a casual brasserie to a table grill where you cook the food yourself.

This is the original — come here for the most authentic Rosenborg experience, far from the shopping center.
Trondheim's first Pilates studio, with reformer training in small groups and close instructor supervision — right in the heart of Nedre Elvehavn.
Ferjemannsveien 4 is literally a few minutes' walk from Scandic Nidelven — perfect for a morning session.
Neighborhood park on Lade — a green pocket within walking distance.
Benches, open lawn and paths — part of Lade's green fabric.
Scandinavian coffee chain with a study-friendly atmosphere — part of Stovner Senter.
Popular for remote working and meetings outside rush hours.

Stjørdal's best address for specialty coffee and natural wine. Run by local microroastery Langøra Kaffe.

Hera Studio on Fjordgata has specialised in hair extensions since 2015, with views toward Munkholmen island and a focus on natural results and precision.
The Fjordgata premises overlook Munkholmen — book early in the week for best availability, as Thursday and Saturday are the most popular days.
Local pastry shop in Asker centre with classic Norwegian cake-making and café atmosphere.
Popular for birthday cakes and Danish pastries. Pick up something for the weekend gathering.
Local bakery in Asker with a strong local connection and traditional production.
Supplies local shops and cafés in the area.
Public library in Laksevåg — quiet reading room, children's section and lending of books and media.
A good alternative to the city centre library for residents west of the centre.
Graffi is an old Trøndelag expression meaning to have real expertise in what you do — and after two decades of spareribs and entrecôte, Graffi Grill Midtbyen lives up to the name.
Sundays bring 20% off the signature Graffi Grillfest dish, and students always get up to 25% discount.
Memorial and learning centre for the 22 July 2011 terrorist attacks — an important part of Norwegian memory.
Free entry. Recommended for teenagers and adults who want to understand contemporary Norway.
Local bakery concept focused on slow-fermented bread and regional ingredients from Western Norway.
Pick up a wholegrain or rye loaf for the week's packed lunches.
An unpretentious burger joint on TMV-kaia that prioritises ingredients over presentation — popular with those wanting something quick between the Solsiden shops.
Ask for the daily recommendation at the counter — it tends to be the freshest combination they have going.
Neighborhood park on Lade — a green pocket within walking distance.
Benches, open lawn and paths — part of Lade's green fabric.
Shopping centre in Frogner with branded and specialist shops in a calm atmosphere.
More exclusive selection than the Majorstuen alternatives — suited to planned shopping trips.

The building is rarely open to the public, but the facade and its placement right next to the cathedral make it a fine photo subject most people walk past.
Apotek 1 at Haugenstua — serving the Haugenstua and Svarttjern neighbourhoods.
Handles both prescriptions and health products for nearby residents.
Founder Paolo Minervini brought Italian cooking to Trondheim in 1973, and Frati has since been the city's go-to reference point for pasta and wine on Kongens gate.

Bryggeriet is a venue in the Ranheim area.
Local option for an evening out in the district.

Long weekday hours until 9 PM — convenient for late evening needs.
A sushi takeaway counter inside the Solsiden shopping centre making fresh sushi to go — convenient for anyone shopping in the area.
Go early in the day for the best selection of pre-packed boxes — the most popular varieties sell out quickly.
Gym with strength, cardio and group classes — a local alternative to the big chains.
Twelve minutes walk from Leangen. Spacious with a personal atmosphere.

value: The building on Kalvskinnet was completed in 1754 as a sugar refinery and is among the country's oldest preserved factory buildings — students now run a pub and concert venue in the cellar.
Check the programme for quiz nights and concerts in the cellar — intimate atmosphere and student-friendly vibes in a historic setting.
Dromedar is Bergen's answer to third-wave coffee — a local concept focused on coffee craft.

YX Skovgård is a restaurant in the Ranheim area.
Local eatery within walking distance from Overvik.

One of the fixtures along the restaurant row on TMV-kaia, known for home-cooked food with quality ingredients and a terrace that catches the afternoon sun on Solsiden.

Forest area on the outskirts of Stjørdal, perfect for a quick woodland walk.
Flat and easy to walk — nice for jogging or a calm nature walk.
Nidaros Boxing Club shares premises with the kickboxing and MMA scene on the third floor of Dora — a raw industrial building by the Nidelva that has become Trondheim's martial arts cluster.
The entrance is next to Kjeldsberg coffee roastery — follow the scent of freshly roasted coffee and you'll find it.
PoMo opened in 2025 inside Trondheim's 1911 Art Nouveau post office, as a new museum of modern and contemporary art spanning 4,000 square metres across five floors.
The museum commits at least 60% of its acquisition budget to women artists — the interiors are designed by India Mahdavi.
Café and restaurant in the Nygårdsparken area — modern Norwegian food in relaxed surroundings.
A good base for a long lunch. Popular with students and university staff.
Flipper Kafe is a local café with homemade food in the Ranheim area.
Quiet stop for lunch or coffee in the middle of the day.
Shopping centre in the Frogner area with a mix of grocery, services and niche shops.
Small and easy to navigate — good for quick everyday errands without going to a larger centre.
The coffee chain's Bakklandet outpost occupies a restored wharf building by the Nidelva and opened in 2014 as their second branch in Trondheim.
The window seats facing the river are the best spots — perfect for a quiet coffee with a view of the Old Town Bridge.
Café and bar in Nøstegaten 106 — low-key neighbourhood spot from morning coffee to evening beer.
A solid choice for a local pint after work without going far.
Spa and massage in the Majorstuen quarter drawing on Asian massage traditions.
Convenient for unwinding after a shopping trip on Bogstadveien.
Interior shop on Wessels veg with Scandinavian design and home furnishings.
Nice for inspiration or a small gift — go with plenty of time.
Egon Solsiden is the chain's Trondheim outpost in the old shipyard area at Nedre Elvehavn, seating around 400 across indoor and outdoor areas.
The quayside terrace is among the most spacious on Solsiden — a safe bet when you need room for a larger group.
Food spot on Hotellgata with a focus on real, good flavors.
Short distance from the hotel — a good everyday alternative.
Bar Moskus is an intimate continental bar on Olav Tryggvasons gate with a small stage for quality concerts, a wide selection of craft beers, and well-crafted cocktails.
Check the concert schedule in advance — the small stage creates an intimacy with the music you won't find elsewhere in the city.
An Indian restaurant in the historic Parkgården building, a space that has housed some of Trondheim's most notable restaurants over the years — now serving spices from the Indian subcontinent.
The tandoori dishes are the safest choice for first-timers — ask for extra naan to mop up the sauces.
EasyFit Buran opened in 2013 and immediately drew a waiting list of new members — since doubled in size, it has become an anchor in the daily rhythm of the Buran neighbourhood.
Three bus stops and a city bike dock sit directly outside, making it a natural first stop whether you commute by public transport or bicycle.
Kebab and grilled dishes at the heart of Stovner Senter.
Known for fast delivery and generous portions.
Natural history museum at UiB — botanical garden, zoological collection and geological exhibition.
The botanical garden is free and open year-round. Museum requires a ticket.
Among Norwegian grocery chains, MENY invests most seriously in fresh produce — a fish counter, meat counter, warm prepared food and hand-cut cheese all under one roof at Moholt.
For those who prioritise ingredients over convenience, MENY Moholt's range of Norwegian specialities and fresh counters brings a quality level that elevates a Monday dinner.
Tram museum near Majorstuen with historic carriages and Oslo transport history.
An unexpected cultural gem for history lovers. Popular with families at weekends.
Art house cinema in Frogner focusing on European film and independent productions.
Small and intimate — a good evening with Norwegian or European quality cinema.
Havnegata 12 sits in the Brattøra area near Pirbadet, Trondheim's major swimming and wellness centre right by the fjord.
A good starting point for exploring the harbour promenade and Brattøra's sculpture park along the waterfront.
Combined skincare studio and hair salon — full beauty service in one place.
Practical for those who want to do both in a single appointment.
Brattørkaia 17C is the address of Powerhouse Brattørkaia, the world's northernmost energy-positive building — it produces more energy than it consumes.
Located right by Trondheim Central Station and the express boat terminal — a useful landmark for navigating the harbour area.
Homemade food and cakes with seasonal ingredients in Torgkvartalet. A natural meeting point in the center.
The lunch menu is solid and quick — order online and pick up ready food with no wait.
Trondheim's most famous coffee chain, with a branch in Torgkvartalet. Hand-brewed coffee and simple pastries.
Quick and reliable morning coffee — the best espresso in the shopping center.
Krambua on Krambugata has a long tradition as Trondheim's cosiest tavern, with everything made from scratch and live blues music on Saturdays.
Operapub on the first Wednesday of each month is a hidden gem — book your table early.
ARA Frisør stays open until 8 PM on weekdays and 7 PM on Saturdays — making it one of the city's most accessible choices for a late haircut.
The salon is child-friendly according to local reviews — practical for families needing a quick trim between activities in the city centre.
A fenced dog park five minutes from the front door — the small amenity that makes life with a dog noticeably better.
The proximity means this isn't a Sunday trip, but part of the daily rhythm.
A wide-ranging department store at Lade for all household needs — Europris is the neighbourhood go-to for affordable interiors, kitchenware, and everyday essentials.
Especially useful during the move-in phase — large selection of storage solutions, tools, and practical items at a fraction of the price.
The neighbourhood pizzeria — pizza and kebab for takeaway or eating in.
A staple of everyday Bønes life. Bønesskogen 40.
Hair salon in Kaigaten — relaxed atmosphere and reliable service.
A good basic salon for the neighbourhood. Quick and efficient.
Hudspesialisten has a dermatologist with a PhD in medical laser treatment — a clinical level you rarely find outside university hospitals.
The recently reopened shop next to the clinic on Olav Tryggvasons gate carries scientifically documented skincare products you won't find in regular stores.
Yoga studio on Kjøpmannsgata with classes for all levels.
Drop-in welcome — a good way to stretch out after traveling.
The music bar at the entrance of Dokkhuset is a regular meeting point for the city's jazz scene, run by Bare Blåbær with room for around 80 guests.
The summer terrace offers views over the Nidelva and the fjord — arrive early on concert nights to secure a spot.
Cultural venue on Søndregata with exhibitions and local events.
A somewhat hidden cultural spot — worth a visit for the curious.

Ciabatta on Kjøpmannsgata is run by the Hofstad sisters with the motto 'something to chew on, something to drink, and nothing to be fooled about' — honest baking, sandwiches, and dinner by Olavshallen.
Perfect for an honest, quick lunch between Olavshallen and Solsiden — the sandwiches are generous.
An unpretentious bar in the Fjordgata strip, where locals and visitors meet in a neighbourhood that has transformed from harbour street to one of the city's most exciting food quarters.
Fjordgata has become Trondheim's most interesting street for food and drink — use Jedi as a starting point for a walk along the strip.
Medical skin clinic on Majorstuen specialised in skin treatments and aesthetic procedures.
Popular with those seeking treatments beyond traditional spa — book well in advance.
An unpretentious Thai restaurant with generous portions and solid vegetarian options – rated 4.6 out of 5 by guests.
Available on both Wolt and Foodora for delivery, but worth dining in for the authentic experience.
A spice-forward restaurant in the Tiller area serving Asian-inspired dishes with bold flavours.
A solid option for those who prefer more heat than what is typically found on Tiller.
A coffee bar inside City Syd partnering with Norway's oldest coffee and tea house – Cup of Excellence coffee roasted at their own roastery in Oslo.
Rated 4.4 out of 5 with over 80 reviews – the fresh baked goods and cakes are well worth a break between shops.
Unique museum for Bergen's buekorps tradition — a district marching tradition dating to the 1800s.
Small and charming museum that illuminates one of Bergen's most distinctive folk customs.
Family-run craft bakery since 1900. Five generations of fresh pastries from their own bakery in the courtyard.
Custard buns and cinnamon rolls are bestsellers — go early for the best selection.
Budget grocery store from the Coop group on Øyanvegen. Good selection at good prices.
The most affordable option in the area — great selection for self-catering at the hotel.
NTNU's humanities library on Kalvskinnet is open daily for NTNU cardholders and houses collections in the humanities, social sciences and the arts.
The reading room is one of the quietest places to work in the city centre — and the library regularly hosts lunch talks called Friminuttet.
A grove-style park with mature trees and genuine quiet — the kind of green space that takes decades to establish.
Well shielded from traffic. That's exactly what makes it a resource, not just a green patch on the map.
Extra supermarket in the neighbourhood — groceries and fresh produce.
Open until 10pm on weekdays. The closest stop for everyday shopping.
Café le Frère on Søndre gate is a classic espresso bar with wood and greenery, often described as Trondheim's best barista café.
Opens at 8 AM on weekdays — a quiet morning option before the streets fill up.
A neighbourhood pub on Møllenberg that opened in December 2024, with cocktails, a wide beer selection and food by Chopsticks — a low-key addition to the area.
Located next to Fretex and Rosenborg Bakeri — combine a thrift-shop find and a pastry with a beer afterwards.
Stu Brattøra is a floating sauna designed by 13 NTNU architecture students — two sauna rooms with fjord views and ice bathing straight off the dock.
Drop-in from 219 NOK or private booking from 1,199 NOK for up to 12 people — you'll receive a door code by SMS after booking.
24/7 fitness center on Stokmovegen with modern equipment and flexible access.
Perfect for those who train at unusual hours — open around the clock.
Norway's oldest art society, founded in 1845 on the initiative of J.C. Dahl, is housed in the former bishop's residence from 1853 with gallery and restaurant right by Nidaros Cathedral.
The ground floor shares space with restaurant Bifrons — you can combine an exhibition with lunch without changing buildings.
Elysian Beauty Lab on Prinsens gate offers microblading and gel nails in an intimate studio setting, earning attention for personal, detail-oriented service.
Book a microblading consultation early — popular slots disappear quickly.
Coop Extra at Lilleby — neighbourhood grocery store.
Low-priced chain focused on everyday goods.
Nordic salon chain known for colouring and treatments — reliable quality and good products.

Pharmacy at the fish market — conveniently located for everyday shopping in the city centre.

Beauty clinic in the centre — aesthetic treatments and skincare with professional expertise.

Olivia Solsiden is the Florence-inspired Italian on the Nidelva riverfront — the first Olivia outside Oslo, with homemade pasta and pizza in an intimate setting for 200 guests.
Ask for the table closest to the river for the best view — and book ahead on weekends.
Neighbourhood convenience store at Persaunet with extended hours and walking distance from Leangen — Coop Prix is the evening solution when Mega has closed.
The nearest bus stop Rønningsbakken is a two-minute walk away — convenient to combine with the commute home.
Catering company based in Stjørdal — named after the nearby village of Hell.
Perfect for ordering food for meetings or events at the hotel.
3T-Ranheim is one of the chain's newest and most modern fitness centres, built in 2016 in the grandstand building at Extra Arena.
Everything from group classes to strength and yoga. Free parking and breakfast deal.
Pharmacy in Bogstadveien with prescriptions, self-care and cosmetics.
Open weekdays and Saturdays. Walk-in for self-care advice.
The standalone Burger King on Tiller – more easily accessible by car than the one inside the shopping centre.
The drive-through makes this a quick stop on the way to or from the E6 motorway, no parking needed.
Lounge is located at Kjøpmannsgata 48, connected to Hotel Grand Olav — a bar lounge centrally placed in the heart of Trondheim's cultural quarter by Olavshallen.
A calm choice for a drink before or after a concert at Olavshallen — walking distance to everything in the center.

Historic city park in Stjørdal center with space for rest and recreation.
Nice for a short break in the middle of the center — benches and green lawns.

Fitness center at Havnegata with modern equipment and flexible opening hours.
Open 24/7 with card access — practical for early morning workouts.
Pons Thai Relax specialises in authentic Thai massage with seasoned therapists, in quiet premises just steps from Møllenberg's café scene.
Try the hot stone treatment after a long day — it's one of their most popular packages.
Trondheim's answer to the bubble tea wave, established in 2022 with Asian snacks and a wide range of tea-based drinks on Olav Tryggvasons gate.
Try one of the warm drinks during winter — the shop also carries a small selection of Korean snacks worth exploring.
The neighbourhood pizza spot at Risenga — affordable and well-loved.
Popular after training at Askerhallen and school days. Free parking.
Handcrafted donuts and coffee in Nøstegaten — a Norwegian take on artisan donut culture.
Popular with the neighbourhood in the morning. The selection changes daily.
Fitness centre on Lade — membership and drop-in options.
Part of the Speed chain with several centres in Trondheim.
Skin and foot care at Stovner Senter — professional treatments without going into the city centre.
A good option for wellness treatments close to home.
MENY at Stovner Senter — wide range, deli counter and wine sales all in one place.
The district's most complete grocery store with over 900 reviews.
2,500 sqm gym across three floors with group training and a naprapath clinic — Stovner's largest.
STOLT has been in the district for 15 years. Over 10% of Stovner municipality employees are members.
Vitusapotek at Stovner Senter — pharmacy with skin care range and personal consultation.
An alternative to Apotek 1 nearby — two pharmacies within walking distance means good access.

Local cultural life right in the neighbourhood. Concerts, lectures and exhibitions.
MENY supermarket in the neighbourhood — groceries and fresh produce.
Open until 10pm on weekdays. The closest stop for everyday shopping.
Originally a naval defence installation to protect against enemy ships, now a lush riverside park south of Nidaros Cathedral with a playground, fitness park and open lawns.
Bring a blanket and sit on the grass facing the river — Marinen is the city's best picnic spot with the cathedral as a backdrop.

The entrance through Sellanraa Books & Bar gives you an easy excuse to arrive with a coffee before settling into the reading rooms.
An American diner on Solsiden inspired by 1930s New York, with sports on the screens, darts and DJs at the weekends.
One of the few places on Solsiden that combines food and entertainment into the late hours — try the dartboard between courses.
Shopping gallery on Bislett with service businesses and shops in historic premises.
Slightly unexpected to find a shopping gallery here — but popular with locals.
Trondheim's only Scottish pub, equally renowned for its aquavit selection as for the hundred-plus whiskies — a warm institution on Søndre gate.

Park and green space in the neighbourhood — 692m from the project.
One of the city's green lungs, accessible on foot.
A small park at the end of Kjøpmannsgata overlooking the Nidelva, Bakklandet and the Old Town Bridge — tucked away between the city-centre streets.

Juice and coffee in the Sirkus area — fresh smoothies and light lunch after shopping.

Cosy corner park in Nøstet — benches and greenery right outside the door.
Good for a quick break from the working day. Charming neighbourhood pocket.

Combined sports ground, playground and park in the neighbourhood.
Versatile outdoor space catering for both play and exercise.
Jakobsli Hårstudio avd. Charlottenlund is a hairdresser in the neighbourhood.
Local hairdresser within walking distance from Overvik.
Coop's budget grocery chain on Østre Rosten, with extended hours that suit those shopping late after work.
Open from 7 AM to 11 PM on weekdays – one of few grocery options in the area with such generous hours.
Kaffebrenneriet on Dronningens gate opened in 2013 as the chain's first outpost outside Oslo, in an Art Nouveau corner where Dronningens gate meets Nordregata — with 20 types of coffee beans.
A prime corner spot for people-watching through large windows.
Godt Brød's Asker branch at Trekanten — sourdough and organic ingredients.

Stjørdal's main shopping center with over 60 shops, cafés, and services. Two minutes' walk from the hotel.
Everything you need under one roof — grocery store, pharmacy, hairdresser, and eateries.
Hair salon in Stjørdal center.

French-inspired beauty salon with facial and body treatments.
