A fresh-food concept inside the Solsiden shopping centre with wraps, smoothies and sushi made from scratch — a quick and relatively healthy option between the shops.
The wraps and smoothies are made on site with clean ingredients — a good choice when you want something lighter in the middle of the day.

Moholt library is open-access from 07:00 to 23:00 — and alongside the books, you can borrow tools and electric cargo bikes. The kind of low-threshold infrastructure that improves daily life without demanding attention.
Having an open-access library 16 minutes away means a quiet reading space, a workshop and an electric cargo bike on standby — a resource many neighbourhoods lack.
Jordbærpikene at Lade is a cozy homestyle café with its own kitchen — known for warm salads, good burgers, and juicy club sandwiches made with fresh seasonal ingredients.
A solid option when you want homemade everyday food without heading into the center — located in the City Lade mall.
A sushi takeaway combining the best of Japanese tradition with a unique presentation – pre-ordering is recommended.
Order hours or days ahead for pick-up at your preferred time – also available via Wolt for delivery.
Trondheim's legendary rock bar since 1985 — two floors with concerts in the basement, pool and darts upstairs, and a regular crowd that has survived four decades.
The basement is the concert venue — check cafe3b.no for the programme, but the top floor works just fine as a relaxed evening pub regardless.
Trondheim's largest conference hotel, built 17 metres into the Nidelva river. Voted Norway's best hotel breakfast fifteen times.
The airport bus stops right outside. Practical for guests and visiting colleagues.
Bar in central Bergen with a solid beer selection and a laid-back atmosphere.
A good option for a round after visiting Bryggen and the fortress.
Rotvollfjæra is a green area in the district.
Great for walks and relaxation in the neighbourhood.
Small skincare clinic with personal service and a focus on natural ingredients.
Good for regular facial care. Small studio — book well in advance.
Cinema in the heart of Vika with comfortable seating and a central location.
Practical if you combine the cinema with a restaurant visit in Vika's dining scene.
Prinsen kinosenter has shown films on Prinsens gate since 1918 when the municipality took over Verdensteateret — today eight screens in a modernised centre owned by Trondheim municipality.
Most international films are shown in their original language with Norwegian subtitles — the Boutiq screens offer a more exclusive experience.
A cosy coffee bar on the ground floor of Sirkus Shopping with fresh open sandwiches, homemade cakes, and a juice bar that takes the fruit press seriously.
Two locations in the same centre — find a quiet corner with candles and plants, and let your weekday lunch feel a touch more civilised.
Trondheim's own bakery since 1902 — production still runs from Rosenborggaten, the range stretching across 600 products. No mystique, just long-practised craft.
Rosenborg is west Trondheim's bread basket, and the Valentinlyst branch is the practical anchor for the daily loop.
The world's first skating museum, dedicated to Norway's skating heritage and Olympic legacy.
Little-known and charming — a good activity for families and sports enthusiasts.
A modern European kitchen in the heart of Kongens gate that transforms Norwegian ingredients with Italian and French finesse — consistently ranked among Trondheim's top restaurants.
Ask for a table on the second floor for a more intimate experience, and let the kitchen choose the menu based on seasonal ingredients.

Trondheim's first specialty coffee bar, founded in 1997 at Bakklandet — Dromedar at Sirkus Shopping brings the city's coffee pioneer heritage to the neighbourhood with its own bakery and Cup of Excellence beans.
The sweet chili drink is the signature — available hot and cold, it has been a local classic since the 90s.
Sculpture park at Rommisletta with outdoor art and a lawn.
The district's outdoor cultural highlight — pleasant for a walk with artistic interest.
The largest fitness center in Trøndelag spans 6,000 square metres across four floors, offering everything from hot yoga to squash and a dedicated spa area.
The newly opened Pilates Reformer studio fits 30 people – unusually for the industry, the reception is staffed during all opening hours.
Pizzabakeren Ranheim — pizza for the people, right in Ranheim.
Quick and affordable. Popular for Friday pizza in the neighbourhood.
Egon The Meat Bazaar is a steak and grill restaurant with a wide menu — steakhouse concept in the centre.
Good for meat-focused diners. Family-friendly and accessible.
Amber wellness centre offers massage, facial treatments and various body treatments.
Book ahead to secure your preferred treatment time.
A small, local bakery in central Trondheim that holds firm to artisan tradition — fresh baked goods made with care every single day.
Arrive early in the morning for the best selection of freshly baked breads and pastries before the most popular items sell out.
The Swedish coffee chain has found its spot in the middle of Trondheim's busiest shopping street — a reliable choice for coffee and wifi when you're on the go in Nordre gate.
The spacious premises make this one of the better downtown spots to find a free seat with a laptop, even during rush hour.
Yoga studio with a calm atmosphere just outside the center. Offers various yoga styles.
Drop-in welcome — check the schedule online to find the right level.
A small, recently established salon on Torvmyra – a personal alternative to the chains inside the shopping centres.
Call 920 95 999 to book – an intimate space with few chairs means closer attention per client.
Classic barber shop in Bergen — cut-throat razor, warm towel and an unhurried old-school service.
One of the city's most talked-about barbers. Book ahead.
Trondheim's oldest boxing club, founded in 1982, trains at Rostenhallen and welcomes everyone from beginners to competitive fighters.
The club regularly hosts Legacy Box Cup tournaments – check their website for training and fight schedules.
An open recreational area with courts for basketball, beach volleyball and ball sports – Tiller's nearest green meeting place.
Part of Tillerparken with outdoor fitness equipment – a welcome break from the commercial district's asphalt.
Founded by an Italian baker and a Norwegian restaurateur in 2019, Hevd merges Nordic sourdough tradition with Italian craft in the Bank Quarter.
Right across from Litteraturhuset — grab a focaccia and settle into the park next door.
Thornæsparken is the Møllenberg neighbourhood's own district park, named after newspaperman, poet and politician Knut Olai Thornæs, and freshly renovated in 2023.
Visit during Møllenberg Day in August for flea markets and neighbourhood gatherings — or any day for flower beds and the playground.
Ølbua is a venue in the Ranheim area.
Local option for an evening out in the district.

Trondheim's only HYROX-approved gym and its most specialised functional fitness facility — here, training is a tool for performing in the world outside the gym. Established in 2007, long before functional training became mainstream.
Five minutes' walk from Brøset: for residents who take everyday performance seriously.
Trondheim's own craft brewery serves tank-fresh beer straight from production alongside award-winning burgers — a gathering point for beer enthusiasts on Søndre gate.
Grab a seat at the bar to watch the brewery in action, and ask the bartenders about seasonal specials that aren't listed on the board.
Nominated Library of the Year — free makerspace, chess club and debates on level 3 of Stovner Senter.
Pride lighthouse and inclusive community space. Open to everyone — from homework help to job-seeking courses.
Apotek 1 at Stovner Senter — quick dispensing of prescriptions and over-the-counter products.
Centrally located near the T-bane and grocery stores.
A little piece of France at Lade — Franske Nytelser was founded in 2005 by Frenchman Denys Favier, baking croissants and sourdough bread with genuine French craft tradition.
The Campaillou bread has become a local bestseller — a rustic French-inspired sourdough worth a detour.
Once part of the Church of Our Lady's churchyard, Tordenskioldsparken has held a bronze statue of naval hero Peter Wessel Tordenskjold since 1876.
The park also holds the Terra Incognita memorial with 77 lights for the victims of July 22nd — a quiet, dignified space beneath ancient trees.
MENY at Trekanten centre — supermarket in the heart of Asker, 70 metres from the train station.
Practical for quick shopping to and from the train. Full range.
The city hotel on Kjøpmannsgata — your starting point for exploring Stjørdal center on foot.
The reception has good tips on local events and seasonal activities.
Godt Brød on Thomas Angells gate bakes everything in-house with mainly organic ingredients, and is ranked Trondheim's top bakery — the glass-roofed backyard café is a favourite on rainy days.
The glass-roofed backyard is a fantastic place to work from with free wifi and good coffee.
A hair salon in the StorM centre offering cuts, colouring, lash and brow tinting.
Located in StorM on Ivar Lykkes veg, with a heated underground garage and 3 hours of free parking.
H2 Nordre on the pedestrian shopping street's most central stretch belongs to the H2 chain — Trondheim's homegrown salon brand with seven locations in the city.
You choose your own price tier based on the stylist's experience level — from Junior to Senior Stylist — smart for any budget.
Extra supermarket in the neighbourhood — groceries and fresh produce.
Open until 10pm on weekdays. The closest stop for everyday shopping.
A strength training studio with 23 years of history on Tiller, open 24/7 – a dedicated environment for serious lifters.
Owner Daniel Dreier has expanded from Tiller to Bergen, Hønefoss and Byneset – but the Tiller location remains the flagship.
Hair salon by the quay — personal service and a varied range of treatments.
poi_name: Studio Milennium Kaien frisør Lamiaa Yousef Hanna

value: Small studio with good atmosphere. Happy to take new clients without a long waiting list.
poi_name: Studio Milennium Kaien frisør Lamiaa Yousef Hanna

value: Tyholttårnet rises 124 metres above Trondheim, and the restaurant at the top completes one full rotation per hour — the city skyline, the fjord and Bymarka in slow panorama. Not an everyday meal; this is where you bring someone visiting for the first time.
Living in the Tyholt neighbourhood means having the city's most recognisable landmark as your nearest viewpoint — an advantage that never loses its effect on guests.
Italian bistro with wood-fired pizza and pasta along Hegdehaugsveien — Frogner's main shopping street.
Good for spontaneous dinner without reservations. Popular with families and couples.
The district library on Majorstuen — open to all, with books, newspapers and quiet workspaces.
Free access. Good for working from home or bringing children for a quiet hour.
Neighborhood park on Lade — a green pocket within walking distance.
Benches, open lawn and paths — part of Lade's green fabric.
Trondheim Yogaskole has taught everything from ashtanga to yin and meditation since 2006 — a small, dedicated school that prizes depth over volume, quietly anchored in the centre of the city.
Alongside open classes, the school runs corporate and institutional courses, making it a natural hub for residents who build stillness and movement into their working week.
Moholt Storsenter is the slightly larger option — MENY, pharmacy, florist and bank gathered around a car park on Vegamot. Functional, local and without unnecessary ambition.
Where Valentinlyst is the neighbourhood centre, Moholt Storsenter is the regional alternative — useful to know when something specific isn't available closer to home.
Pharmacy in Bislett with prescriptions, self-care and cosmetics.
Open weekdays and Saturdays. Walk-in for self-care advice.
The pharmaceutical wholesaler behind the Vitusapotek chain, with a distribution centre serving pharmacies across the region.
Not a public pharmacy, but the infrastructure ensuring that Tiller's pharmacies always have medicines in stock.
Oslo's largest cinema at Colosseum Center — wide repertoire of blockbusters and premieres.
Easy parking. Pairs well with dinner in the Colosseum quarter.
A café on Brattørkaia where the old harbor district has transformed into one of the city's most modern neighborhoods — a perfect pit stop between student life and the fjord promenade.
Take your coffee along the Brattørkaia promenade for one of the downtown area's finest fjord walks with views toward Munkholmen.
Trondheim's oldest taekwondo club, founded in 1982 and named with the Korean word for "the path to the goal" – based on Østre Rosten.
The club moved to Tiller in 1999 and welcomes all levels – from beginners who have never kicked to experienced practitioners.
Pub and cultural venue at Kjøpmannsgata 38 with live music and local atmosphere.
Check the program for live music — a hangout for music-loving Stjørdal locals.
Neighbourhood convenience store at Persaunet with extended hours and walking distance from Leangen — Coop Prix is the evening solution when Mega has closed.
The nearest bus stop Rønningsbakken is a two-minute walk away — convenient to combine with the commute home.
A neighbourhood restaurant that earns loyalty through flavour rather than fanfare — pizza and pasta with the relaxed repetition that turns a local favourite into somewhere you actually return to.
Nearly 400 Google reviews aren't accidental: Viva Italia is where you go when you don't want to cook and don't want to wait.
Central Norway's leading budget fitness chain holds FITcert Level 4 — Europe's highest gym certification — with more than 14,000 members across ten branches in the Trondheim region.
A wallet-friendly alternative to the pricier centres nearby, with modern equipment and a no-frills focus on self-guided training.
Asker library in the Cultural Centre at Trekanten — books, quiet workspaces, and cultural events.
Free access and open most days. Great for students and booklovers.
Asker Cinema with modern screens — Nordisk Film's venue right next to Trekanten.
Easy to combine with dinner in Asker centre. Always an up-to-date programme.
"Terra Incognita" in Tordenskioldsparken by Vår Frue church — 77 points of light in a white concrete archipelago commemorating the values attacked on July 22, 2011.
Visit after dark, when the 77 lights reflect in the shallow pool and create a quiet, contemplative starry sky.
Sumo is Bergen's best-known sushi chain — Japanese-inspired food in relaxed surroundings.
Good for a quick lunch. The combo menu is value for money.
CrossFit box in the Bryggen district — high-intensity strength and conditioning in community.
Drop-in possible. Warm and inclusive atmosphere even for beginners.
Seasonally driven menu in an intimate setting — Norwegian seafood and local ingredients at Øvre Korskirkeallmenning.
Book a table. Three choices per course or a full tasting menu.
The hotel's own bistro with a modern twist on classic dishes and Italian-inspired small plates – open to everyone, not just hotel guests.
Open Monday to Saturday 6–10 PM and Sundays 1–4 PM – one of few dining spots on Tiller with a bistro atmosphere.
A public urban space at Havnegata in Trondheim's harbor area — part of the ongoing renewal transforming the quay into a vibrant hub between fjord and city.
A good starting point for a walk along the harbor promenade, with views over the Trondheim Fjord and proximity to Pirbadet and Pirsenteret.
Kafé Larssen on Fjordgata is a classic Trondheim dive bar with local craft beers, live music, and trivia nights — a local haunt where everyone knows each other.
Check the schedule for live bands on Fridays and Saturdays — unpretentious and always a good time.
Nobel Peace Prize museum at Aker Brygge, telling the story behind every prize since 1901.
Interactive exhibitions and the current year's laureate highlighted. Popular with international visitors.
Neighbourhood park — green breathing space 5 minutes' walk from Stovner Torg.
Popular for morning walks and lunchtime strolls.
Backstube's Nordre gate outpost is a dependable stop for European pastries in the heart of Trondheim's busiest shopping street.
Available via Wolt with 15–25 minute delivery if you prefer breakfast in your hotel room.
An enlarged Lewis chess piece carved in soapstone at 12:1 scale — the shield biter with its characteristic staring eyes guards the courtyard in front of the Archbishop's Palace.
Notice the crooked gaze and the long beard curling over the shield — the sculpture was originally created as a mascot for the Olavsaften festival in 2020.
Small freshwater lake at Knappen — natural starting point for hikes in the Bønes hills.
A peaceful lake surrounded by forest. Well suited for short trips with children.
Regnbueplassen is Bergen's LGBTQ+ corner — colourful tiles and an open, inclusive atmosphere.
A gathering point during Pride and throughout the summer months.
Martial arts club on Kjøpmannsgata for kickboxing and self-defense.
Check if they offer trial sessions for visitors — active and inclusive club.
Hair salon in Stjørdal center.
Book an appointment in advance — drop-in can be difficult on weekends.
Klinikk Veronika AS is a hairdresser in the neighbourhood.
Local hairdresser within walking distance from Overvik.
Pharmacy centrally on Kjøpmannsgata with a wide selection and advisory services.
Has most of what you need in health and wellness products within walking distance.
Norway's national museum of music — set at historic Ringve manor.
A collection of instruments from around the world, with an adjoining botanical garden.
Northern Europe's oldest rock club (1969) — carved out of the mountain beneath Nygårdshøyden.
Legendary live music venue run by volunteers. The underground atmosphere is intact.
EVO fitness centre in Asker centre — complete facility with strength, cardio and studio spaces.
Popular among commuters and Asker residents. Good accessibility from the station.
Trondheim Film Club operates out of Cinemateket, curating screenings for just 100 NOK per semester — the city's most dedicated film community.
A membership card costs 100 NOK per semester and includes the first screening — the rest are 50 NOK each, well below regular cinema prices.
Asian-inspired sushi with a Norwegian twist inside City Syd – a sushi buffet with varied selection and locally sourced ingredients where possible.
Reserve a table before arriving – the sushi buffet is popular and fills up fast, especially on Saturdays.
Neighborhood recreation area east of Meieriveien with trails and green space.
Nice for an evening walk in quiet residential streets.
Norway's only museum of deaf culture and history, in the red 1855 building that originally housed the country's oldest school for the deaf — a unique window into an often invisible cultural heritage.
All information is available in Norwegian sign language and text, making the museum equally accessible for hearing and deaf visitors.
Norway's answer to quick, simple food right by Trondheim Central Station — a familiar stop for travelers needing fuel between trains and buses at Fosenkaia.
Strategically located right by the central station, this is among the first eateries you encounter when arriving in Trondheim by train.
A salon and barbershop with two distinct personalities — holding an exacting standard for precision and premium products from Keune, Reuzel and Proraso.
The closest thing to a full-service barbershop at neighbourhood scale: the men's cut that has actually been thought through.
Grilled dishes and kebab within walking distance of Stovner Torg.
High rating with a loyal clientele from nearby workplaces.
Turkish grill and steakhouse with halal-certified kitchen and a chef with 30 years of experience.
Over 450 sqm with generous portions and rich flavours — one of the district's most reviewed restaurants.
Trondheim's premier English pub since 2005, run by Brits with a passion for authentic pub culture — from fish and chips to live football and weekly quiz nights.
The Thursday quiz is an institution — come alone and get placed on a team, or bring your own crew for one of the city's most sought-after pub nights.
Asker's most loved coffee bar, rated #1 in the city. Lippe coffee and organic pastries from Godt Brød.
Best place to start the day — opens 07:30 weekdays, 08:00 Saturday. 114 metres from Asker station.
Wellbeing salon in the neighbourhood with massage and beauty treatments.
A local favourite for relaxation — book online.
Gym in the Majorstua quarter with a broad class timetable and modern equipment.
Popular among 20–40-year-olds in the area. Good capacity for spinning and strength sessions.
EVO gym on Oscarsgate — central location for residents of Frogner and Majorstuen.
Access to free parking in the evenings. Good for interval training and free weights.
One of Trondheim's best-known café chains at its prime location right by the main square — fresh salads, sandwiches, and a casual atmosphere in the heart of city life.
Perfect for a quick lunch between Torget and Munkegata, with outdoor seating that catches the afternoon sun during the warmer months.
Laugaren is a community-built floating sauna moored at USF Verftet — DOGA award winner 2023.
Volunteer-run and membership-based. Book a spot at laugaren.no.
Espresso House at Trondheim Torg, right by the main square — a central café hub in the pedestrian street where the city's commerce and culture converge.
The location right by Torvet makes this a natural meeting point, and the premises work well as a base between errands in Midtbyen.
Småbergan is Trondheim's largest park at roughly 120 acres, wrapping around Kristiansten Fortress with 360-degree views of fjord, city and mountains.
The municipality has leased the area from the state since 1897 — bring a picnic and walk the Defence Trail for the city's best panorama.
Hair salon on Kjøpmannsgata with a focus on modern cuts and coloring.
Book online — popular salon that is often fully booked.
A cocktail bar on Solsiden's lively TMV quay that combines nightclub energy with bartending craft — at the core of Trondheim's most urban nightlife district.
Sundays draw the student crowd for a relaxed start to the week, while Fridays and Saturdays see a packed dance floor as the evening progresses.
A bar on Ferjemannsveien in the Solsiden area, established in 2015 — part of the ever-growing nightlife scene in the old industrial quarter by the Nidelva river.
Solsiden's many bars and restaurants are packed close together, making this a natural stop on an evening stroll along the quay.
Modern cinema in Kimen cultural center, the heart of Stjørdal's cultural life. From blockbusters to local events.
Check the program at kimenkino.no — the cultural center also hosts exhibitions and concerts worth a visit.
Established hair salon in Laksevåg with a loyal local following.
Good for those who want to escape the city centre bustle. Easy parking nearby.
Popular fitness center on Ole Vigs gate with varied offerings and good atmosphere.
Ask about drop-in prices — multiple group classes available throughout the week.
Authentic Italian pizza and pasta on Solsiden since 2014 — one of Trondheim's highest-rated Italian restaurants, where ingredients and love for the craft are at the core.
In summer, the large outdoor terrace facing Beddingen is among the most sought-after spots in the city — arrive early to secure a seat in the sun.
A casual bar and kitchen on Kongens gate serving world-inspired comfort food — from pizza and steam buns to the daily catch, with room for both weeknight dinners and celebrations.
Saturday brunch with eggs benedict is a local favorite, and the venue can be booked for private events with a full technical setup.
Diskoteket is Trondheim's most stubborn dance floor — a nightclub on Carl Johans gate with over 12 beers on tap and a mix of house, techno, and disco keeping the city awake.
Show up early on weekdays for bingo and cheap beer — weekends belong to the dancers.
The bakery behind Byåsen Bakeri – Nærbakst took over the nearly 100-year-old tradition in 2009 and carries it forward with handmade cakes.
The bakery on Østre Rosten supplies bread and cakes to outlets in Tiller, Heimdal, Stavset and Munkvoll.
A heritage bakery tracing its roots to Köhlers Conditori in 1931 – the marzipan and cream cakes remain bestsellers.
Local specialities like georginekake, romkake and lukket valnøtt are still baked according to the original recipes.
Pascal Konditori on Søndre gate brings the French patisserie to Trondheim — macarons, truffles, croissants, and croque monsieur right next to the Nye Hjorten Theater.
Order weekend cakes by Thursday — the full range of Pascal pastries is available for pickup Friday through Sunday.
Onkel Svanhild is ranked Trondheim's best bakery on TripAdvisor — opened in 2020 as a dream come true for founder Trond Vardehaug Thuen, with breakfast and lunch in the city center.
Come early for fresh pastries — the most popular items are often sold out by lunch.
Relax Space on Havnegata is within walking distance of Nedre Elvehavn — the district born when the TMV shipyard closed in 1983 and the old workshop halls found new purpose.
A perfect pit stop after a long walk along the Nidelva wharves.
Thai restaurant in the neighbourhood — classic dishes.
Popular for takeaway and dine-in with Lade locals.
The main square in Stjørdal center — meeting place for market days and local events.
Check if it's market day — local producers sell seasonal goods here regularly.
A dining spot inside Norway's largest water park by the harbor — open to everyone, including non-swimmers, with views over the Trondheim Fjord.
You don't need a swimming ticket to eat here — walk straight into the café for a casual lunch with fjord views without going through the changing rooms.
Café and gallery in Hollendergaten — vegetarian kitchen and rotating art exhibitions.
A good option for lunch with a cultural edge. Vegetarian dishes and eco-friendly choices.
An open meadow that enables what people don't need to plan: spontaneous football, free play, or simply lying in the grass.
Open flat terrain is rare in denser neighbourhoods. Here it exists — thirteen minutes away.
Walk of Peace is a series of memorial stones along Dronningens gate, created by Åshild Herdlevær in 2011, honouring winners of the Student Peace Prize during ISFiT.
Every other year the walk is extended with a new stone — a discreet but meaningful outdoor exhibition you can easily pass without noticing.
Crispy Fried Chicken Trondheim Øst is a restaurant in the Ranheim area.
Local eatery within walking distance from Overvik.
Spa and wellness in Torgkvartalet — treatments right in the center.
Combine shopping with a well-deserved treatment — all under one roof.
Daglig Deig is Italian bakery founder Stefano Matarese's latest project on Bakklandet — fresh pasta, freshly baked bread, and sweet delicacies with genuine Italian craftsmanship.
Come on Thursday evening for unlimited pasta — a weekly all-you-can-eat pasta night that's become a local favorite.

Trondheim's first specialty coffee bar, founded in 1997 at Bakklandet — Dromedar at Sirkus Shopping brings the city's coffee pioneer heritage to the neighbourhood with its own bakery and Cup of Excellence beans.
The sweet chili drink is the signature — available hot and cold, it has been a local classic since the 90s.
Founded in 1880. A cultural institution near Frogner Park, with 915 artworks on the walls and 249 beers on the menu.
Parkveien 12 — a haunt for artists, journalists and locals since the late 19th century.
Massage studio on Kirkevegen with a focus on relaxation and muscle treatment.
Appointment recommended — calm and professional treatment.
Boots at Valentinlyst combines pharmacy with the wider shopping centre offering — practical when you're already heading that way.
Eight minutes away. Part of a Valentinlyst trip, not necessarily a trip in itself.
Modern public library in Kimen cultural center with reading areas, group rooms, and free wifi.
A quiet retreat with newspapers, books, and workstations — perfect on a rainy day.
Restaurant Romantica is a long-established pizzeria at Ranheim with loyal guests.
A regular neighbourhood restaurant for many families in the district.

Norway's northernmost synagogue also houses a museum gifted to Trondheim for the city's 1000th anniversary in 1997 — telling the story of Jewish life north of Dovre through thousands of photographs and artifacts.
The former 1864 railway station housing the synagogue is an architectural highlight in itself — take a moment to study the building's facade before entering.
Aesthetic clinic in Bergen centre — face and skin treatments using evidence-based methods.
poi_name: Din Kosmetiske Klinikk | Hudpleie Bergen Sentrum

value: Book a consultation. Good reputation for professional treatment.
poi_name: Din Kosmetiske Klinikk | Hudpleie Bergen Sentrum

value: City park right next to Kimen cultural center. Gathering point for events and daily life.
Nice for a short break between the cinema and the library — central and green.
Extra Rosenborg is the neighbourhood grocery for Nedre Elvehavn residents and hotel guests — everyday essentials within walking distance of Solsiden.
Open until 11 PM Monday to Saturday, but closed Sundays — plan your evening shop accordingly.
Jacob's supermarket in the neighbourhood — groceries and fresh produce.
Open until 10pm on weekdays. The closest stop for everyday shopping.
Relaxed neighbourhood restaurant on St. Hanshaugen with seasonal kitchen and good wine list.
Lively atmosphere in the evening — works just as well as a bar as a restaurant.
Trondheim's first brewpub since 1998, and the city's first craft distillery — all beer is brewed on-site on Prinsens gate, right in the city center.
Ask to taste the exclusive brews only served here that never reach store shelves — the bartenders are happy to share the stories behind each recipe.
Fitnesspoint is a self-service gym chain with 39 locations across Norway, and the Pirsenteret branch gives you a workout with harbour views in Trondheim's maritime heart.
Self-service means flexible training hours — perfect for business travellers with unpredictable schedules.
Coffee Buddies on Jomfrugata is a low-key café stop on one of the city centre's quieter side streets, just behind the main-street buzz.
A solid alternative for those who want to avoid queues at the more well-known cafés.
A budget department store with a broad everyday selection – the Pluss concept means a larger range than standard Europris outlets.
Located on Ivar Lykkes veg next to TillerTorget, with convenient parking right outside.
Trekanten is Asker's urban shopping centre with over 3.3 million visits in 2023 — 70 metres from the train station.
MENY, H&M, Clas Ohlson and Asker Mathall all in one place. Cultural centre and cinema next door.
City museum at Frogner Manor, covering Oslo's urban history from the 10th century to today.
Nice to combine with a visit to Vigeland Park right next door.
Frøken Fryd is a small oasis for skin and body care run by therapist Tonje Karlsen — with Dermalogica and Jane Iredale on the shelves.
An intimate one-person clinic means undivided attention — call 93 40 78 78 to book, as online booking is limited.
A health-focused café on Fjordgata specializing in protein-rich smoothies and nutritious bowls — Trondheim's answer to a healthier alternative in the city center.
A popular lunch spot for downtown workers who want something lighter — order through the app to skip the queue during the lunch rush.
Park and green space in the neighbourhood — 1178m from the project.
One of the city's green lungs, accessible on foot.
Resource center on Værnesgata focusing on sustainability and transition in the local community.
poi_name: Ro Ressurssenter for omstilling i Kommun

value: Regularly hosts workshops and talks — check the program for open events.
poi_name: Ro Ressurssenter for omstilling i Kommun

value: Hair salon in Stjørdal center.
Book an appointment in advance — drop-in can be difficult on weekends.
TKM Gråmølna combines an 1840 steam mill built by Anders Graae with a modern 2008 extension — housing, among other works, the Håkon Bleken art gift.
The ground floor is shared with Nordenfjeldske Kunstindustrimuseum, so you get two museums in one visit — open Thursday to Sunday.
Trondheim's rebellious little sister of the restaurant scene, led by Top Chef winner Reneé Fagerhøi — surprise menu, flamingo decor, and Frank Ocean on the speakers.
You won't get a menu in advance — surrender to the kitchen's choices and let yourself be surprised by six to ten courses blending local seafood with unexpected comfort food.
Strength training studio on Wessels veg. For those who like raw and focused workouts.
More specialized than the chains — popular among local powerlifters.
A food shop in the Tiller area focused on fresh ingredients and local products.
An alternative to the big chains for those who value a personal, curated food selection.
French patisserie in Nøstegaten — Baptiste from France baked this little bakery into the neighbourhood.
Visit after the sauna at Verftet. Gluten-free options and croissants that rival Paris.
Wood-fired pizza at City Syd with fresh salads and a family-friendly atmosphere – pizzas with Mickey Mouse ears for the little ones.
All pizzas can be made vegetarian, and prices range from 200–300 kr per person – ordering via Wolt is also available.
Nova houses Trondheim's largest screen — the 431-seat Liv Ullmann auditorium with Dolby Atmos and 4K — plus two boutique cinemas with velvet sofas.
Book Nova 2 or Nova 3 BOUTIQ for exclusive velvet seats and cushioned sofas — the most comfortable cinema experience in the city.
Apollo Hårsenter on Kjøpmannsgata is part of Norway's largest hair loss network, with five specialists and more than 30 years of expertise.
Offers free scalp analysis and custom solutions — from hair systems to wigs and scalp treatments.
Fresh Fitness by Bakke Bru is a newly renovated budget gym with a near-24/7 feel — open from 5 AM to midnight, 365 days a year.
From 249 NOK/month with no contract — the most affordable option within walking distance of Solsiden.
Vitusapotek Byhaven is located in the 32-shop mall on Olav Tryggvasons gate — Trondheim's most central shopping stretch.
Convenient if you're already in the city centre — open until 6 PM on weekdays.
Stiftsgårdsparken is the garden behind Scandinavia's largest wooden palace, originally laid out in Rococo style from drawings by Johan Daniel Berlin.
The park was reconstructed for Trondheim's millennium in 1997 and features a statue of King Olav V — entrances from both Torvet and Dronningens gate.
Gola Gelato started in Argentina 27 years ago, passed through Spain, and landed on Fjordgata in 2019 — handcrafted gelato with local milk and Argentine empanadas.
Try the combo of gelato and homemade empanadas — an unexpected fusion that works surprisingly well.
A brasserie on the ninth floor of the Clarion Hotel with panoramic views over the Trondheim Fjord — Nordic gastronomy meets modern European cuisine high above the wharves.
Ask for a window seat facing the fjord for the best view, and consider the Chef's Choice menu to let the kitchen showcase its finest.
Full-range supermarket at Sirkus Shopping with fresh fish and meat counters — Coop Mega covers everything from weekday essentials to weekend dinner ingredients.
The first hour of parking at Sirkus Shopping is free — easy to combine a big grocery run with other errands in the mall.
Bistro and bar by Bislett stadium — a hub for the neighbourhood's food scene.
Lively on Fridays and weekends. Easy to drop in after a walk.
ULF-AN bokseklubb offers fitness in the Ranheim area.
Fitness option within walking distance from Overvik.
Nose-to-tail restaurant in Fosswinckels gate — local ingredients and sustainable choices from fjord and soil.
Sharing plates and a solid natural wine selection. Its popularity means you should book a table.
Scandinavia's first brewpub, opened in 1989 on Bogstadveien. All beers brewed in-house.
Fermentation tanks visible from the bar — from light lager to Belgian-style and stout, all in one place.
A fitness centre run by physiotherapists with specialist expertise in medical exercise and rehabilitation.
Training programmes are regularly reviewed by healthcare professionals – a solid choice for those needing tailored follow-up.
A health centre at Heimdal offering physiotherapy, chiropractic care and shockwave treatment – all under one roof.
Heimdal station is an 8-minute walk away, with good bus and train connections from Tiller.
Small café in a historic building with views over Trondheimsfjorden.
Local and homemade fare — 4.9-star reviews from guests.
A casual eatery on Havnegata with a playful name rooted in Trøndelag dialect humor and honest, simple food — right next to Scandic Nidelven.
The name plays on local Trøndelag dialect and humor — a place that doesn't take itself too seriously, but delivers solid everyday food.
Extra Charlottenlund is recently renovated and reopened with a new store concept. Wide selection at low prices.
Nearest large grocery store from Overvik. Good selection and parking.
La Bella Pizzeria AS is a restaurant in the Ranheim area.
Local eatery within walking distance from Overvik.
Indoor activity hall in an old mountain hall. Unique setting for training and events.
Check what's on — the hall is used for everything from climbing to concerts.
New 24/7 gym at Tyholttårnet with two floors and spacious facilities.
Budget-friendly with flexible membership — train whenever it suits you, no commitment.
A cozy cafe at Sirkus Shopping with homemade cakes and open-faced sandwiches in a candlelit, plant-filled setting — Krem is the neighbourhood's informal living room.
The cakes are baked on-site and rank among the area's best — combine lunch and a coffee break in one visit.
Budget-friendly hairdresser on Majorstuen with fast service, no appointment required.
poi_name: Adams Frisør | Beste og billigste frisør på Majorstuen

value: Walk-ins welcome. Good for a quick haircut without a long wait.
poi_name: Adams Frisør | Beste og billigste frisør på Majorstuen

value: The Moholt pharmacy serves the student district and wider neighbourhood. Functions as the local option for a large part of the east side.
Accessibility is what matters most — and it is accessible.
Local convenience store at Vestli — a quick stop for everyday shopping.
Serves the Vestli neighbourhood with a central location.
Park and green space in the neighbourhood — 331m from the project.
One of the city's green lungs, accessible on foot.
Facials and skin treatments focused on results — individually tailored programmes.
Recommended for those serious about skincare. Book a consultation.
Høybråten and Stovner sports club's forest cabin café in Gjelleråsmarka — open on Sundays.
Start from Vestli T-bane. Simple refreshments, a children's ski slope, and an ancient pilgrim route nearby.
The pharmacy on Kongens gate sits at one of the city centre's most-walked corners, a practical constant in the dense neighbourhood fabric around Trondheim Torg.
The pharmacy carries a curated skincare range including Dermalogica and La Roche-Posay, useful to know if you prefer not making separate trips to specialist boutiques.
Trondheim's first cocktail club, opened in 2023 on Fjordgata — a place where festive elegance, musical joy, and exceptional cocktails converge under one roof.
Come early to savor cocktails at a leisurely pace, and stay as the dance floor opens up through the evening — BLDR is pronounced "Bolder" and lives up to the name.
The Valentinlyst anchor store, with a broad range stretching from the Anglamark own brand to fresh produce — and you can collect your post in the same trip.
Seven minutes on foot from Brøset, with generous free parking and EV charging: the neighbourhood supermarket that takes its role seriously.

I. Grande Frisør at Valentinlyst Centre is a rare standout in a category too often defined by anonymity: a spacious, bright salon with experienced professionals offering everything from cuts to extensions.
The neighbourhood's practical salon choice for the whole family, with a level of craft that exceeds expectations for a shopping centre location.
3T — Norway's largest gym chain, with a branch on Lade.
Fully equipped centre with group classes, next to City Lade.
Coop Mega supermarket in the neighbourhood — groceries and fresh produce.
Open until 10pm on weekdays. The closest stop for everyday shopping.
The city center's most accessible grocery store on Kongens gate — a Coop Extra covering everything from fresh produce to parcel pickup, right on the pedestrian street.
One of few downtown stores with extended hours and a broad selection — also functions as a parcel pickup point for those living or working in Midtbyen.
Trøndelag's leading gym chain since 2003, with this center centrally located on Kongens gate — certified with Europe's highest standard for fitness centers.
The center opens early in the morning, making it a popular stop for a pre-work session among those living and commuting in the city center.
Velbehag on Fjordgata 9b belongs to Norway's fastest-growing medical skincare chain, founded in 2021 — offering everything from botox and fillers to dermapen and foot care.
The clinic is in a reddish building to the left of the Trøndelag Centre for Contemporary Art — street parking right outside.
AiSuma on Kjøpmannsgata serves Mediterranean-inspired dishes with an extra focus on steak and barbecue, offering front-row views of the Nidelva river.
Reserve your table well ahead, especially on weekends — and note they close from late June to mid-July.
Hair studio in the city centre specialising in colour and contemporary cuts.
A good address for those who value a current look.
Norway's oldest scientific library, with roots back to 1768 — open to everyone, not just students.
Fifteen campus libraries under one umbrella, with special collections and reading rooms that make it a quiet sanctuary in the heart of a university city.
Shopping center on Sandgata with a wide selection of shops and services.
A good complement to Torgkvartalet — more unique shops here.
Local hairdresser at Stovner Senter — neighbourhood service for the locals.
Small and personal — regular customers are valued.
Handcrafted burgers with local ingredients on Søndre gate — part of the Hammerhead family and a strong contender for the title of Trondheim's best burger.
Shares premises with Hammerhead brewery, so pair a burger with a tank-fresh beer from the brewery next door for the complete experience.

One of Norway's oldest museums, founded in 1826 as "The Historical Hall of Arms" — displayed in the Archbishop's Palace which served military purposes for over 300 years, with artifacts from the Viking Age to World War II.
Combine your visit with the Archbishop's Palace's other exhibitions and Nidaros Cathedral right next door — the entire area deserves a couple of unhurried hours.
Local café and catering venue at Haugenstua — home-made food in quiet surroundings.
A 15-minute walk from Stovner Torg — a good destination for weekend coffee.
Hair salon in Stjørdal center.
Book an appointment in advance — drop-in can be difficult on weekends.
An authentic Italian hole-in-the-wall near Persaunet — Il Fornaio bakes pizza in a MAM oven from Modena with ingredients shipped directly from Italy.
The dough follows a ciabatta recipe that yields an airy, crisp crust — a technique rarely found in Norwegian pizzerias.
Park and green space in the neighbourhood — 347m from the project.
One of the city's green lungs, accessible on foot.
Flex Gym on Lade — a local training alternative.
Lower threshold than the big chains, with a local feel.
Trondheim's only studio for Iyengar yoga, on the third floor of Kjøpmannsgata with views over the Old Town Bridge — taught by certified instructors with three years of training.
The view over Lykkens Portal and the Nidelva river from the studio provides a uniquely special setting for practice — check for drop-in availability before heading up.
One of seven Trondheim locations built around a single premise: that exercise should fit your life, not the other way around. Unstaffed, always open, no binding period.
For residents who want flexibility without sacrificing proximity: TrenHer is within walking distance.
Park and green space in the neighbourhood — 166m from the project.
One of the city's green lungs, accessible on foot.
Hair salon inside Sirkus Shopping — conveniently placed for a cut while running errands.
Nine minutes walk from Leangen. Located centrally in the mall, easy to combine with other errands.
Norwegian chicken from local farms, breaded and fried using original recipes. A local alternative to fast-food chains.
CFC Tenders and Nuggets Bucket are local favorites — order via Wolt for delivery to the hotel.
Frisør Picasso on Thomas Angells gate is a small, experienced salon with four stylists — the kind of place where you get the same quality without the brand premium.
Opens at 9 AM and sits right by the main square — perfect for an early trim before starting your day in the centre.
ISAK occupies Trondheim's old town hall by the library, baking sourdough with ancient grains from Gullimunn — paired with tea from Norway's only Master Tea Blender.
Order the tea from Gravraak Teatelier — it's as considered as the bread.
Full-range pharmacy in the centre — medicines, health foods and skincare products.
Good for quick service. Prescriptions filled without waiting in quieter periods.
Bergen Flyt specialises in flotation therapy — sensory deprivation in a saltwater tank.
Closed pods and open pool variant available. Good for stress reduction.
Local hair salon in the Engen district with an established following among city centre residents.
Worth recommending for cuts and colour. Safe pair of hands.
Historic bathing facility in the Bislett quarter with swimming pool, gym and wellness offerings.
Open to all — among Oslo's oldest and most-used bathing and fitness facilities.
Boots Apotek on Nordre gate sits in the middle of Trondheim's pedestrian street, offering everything from prescriptions to health checks like cholesterol and blood pressure screening.
Open until 6 PM on weekdays and 4 PM on Saturdays — closed Sundays.
Barry's is the global group training concept that came to Bergen — treadmill and bar work in a dark studio.
Book ahead to secure a spot. An intense experience for those who want to push themselves.
A cozy cafe at Sirkus Shopping with homemade cakes and open-faced sandwiches in a candlelit, plant-filled setting — Krem is the neighbourhood's informal living room.
The cakes are baked on-site and rank among the area's best — combine lunch and a coffee break in one visit.
Trondheim's own bakery since 1902 — Rosenborg Bakeri was started by master baker Magnus Helgesen and is now run by the fourth generation with over 600 products.
The Sirkus Shopping branch is closest to Leangen — a perfect stop for fresh rolls and coffee during the shopping run.

Named after one of Trondheims first major cinemas from 1910, Kosmorama has grown since 2005 into Central Norways most important film festival — an annual celebration of international cinema in the heart of the city.
Screenings take place across several city-center cinemas, so check the programme early to secure tickets for the most sought-after films.
Norway's largest pharmacy chain with a branch on Kjøpmannsgata. Open late on weekdays.
Useful for over-the-counter medicine and travel essentials — short walk from the hotel.
A massage and wellness centre in Heimdal offering everything from traditional Thai massage to aromatherapy.
Located in Heimdal centre, a short bus ride from Tiller – a quieter alternative to the shopping centre options.
Trondheim's main library comprises three buildings — the old Town Hall, Lorck Manor, and the 1988 addition — making it Norway's third-largest public library.
Enter via Sellanraa bok & bar for a seamless transition between coffee, bookshop and the library's three floors.
Trondheim's largest gym chain with eight locations — FITcert Level 4-certified and open nearly around the clock.
The Leuthenhaven centre on Kongens gate is the most central, with free coffee, weekday breakfast and training guidance included in every membership.
Olav Tryggvasons gate is the northernmost of the five east-west axes Cicignon drew after the great fire of 1681 — still the main artery through Midtbyen and the citys natural meeting point.
Best explored on foot, where side streets and narrow alleyways reveal unexpected shops and cafes hidden behind the facades.
WeightWellness offers fitness in the Ranheim area.
Fitness option within walking distance from Overvik.

The National Museum of Decorative Arts houses one of Norways finest collections of craft and design, with an entire floor dedicated to the pioneering work of Hannah Ryggen, Synnove Anker Aurdal and Benny Motzfeldt.
The museum recently reopened in Munkegata after years of renovation — a quiet alternative to the more visited attractions downtown.
The University's cultural history museum in the centre, with Viking Age and Norwegian heritage exhibitions.
A good first stop for newcomers who want to understand Oslo's deep history.
NTNU Art Academy Library, in Industribygget at Innherredsveien 7, has been part of the university library since 1997, serving the city's fine art education.
Everyone is welcome to use the library and borrow books — a quiet retreat on Solsiden with a strong art collection.
Scandinavian non-profit gym movement focused on affordable, accessible group training.
No lock-in contracts, low monthly fees and a wide class menu for all levels.
Stovner Senter — the district's shopping hub with over 60 shops, restaurants and services.
A 5-minute walk from Stovner Torg. Groceries, pharmacy, gym and restaurants all in one building.
Natural rocky outcrop and green space at Tukerud — a short walk with views over the neighbourhood.
Good terrain for a quick nature break from the daily routine.
A family business since 2018 with its own bakehouse on Flatåsen and a café at TillerTorget – Trønder svele made to their own recipe is the signature.
Try the homemade, thick sveler with butter and brown cheese – baked fresh and delivered daily from the bakehouse on Flatåsen.
Local pizza restaurant in Stovner — a homely alternative to chain food.
Popular for family dinners and neighbourhood takeaway.
Akimi offers group fitness and personal training at Askerhallen.
Known for motivating instructors and a strong social atmosphere.
SATS Asker — Norway's leading fitness chain with a complete centre downtown.
Great group classes and broad schedule. Convenient location near Trekanten.
Ytre Kongsgard takes its name from the Reformation in 1537, when the archbishops estate became crown property — today an open public space with medieval history underfoot.
The square hosts concerts and events throughout the year, but works equally well as a quiet breathing space between Nidaros Cathedral and the city center.
Spontan Vinbar is the little sibling of restaurant Saga — Michelin-recommended, with natural wine, entrecôte, and a casual drop-in atmosphere on Fjordgata 1.
The wine bar is drop-in only, no reservation needed — try the cheese and charcuterie plate with a glass of natural wine.
A beauty clinic on Tiller specialising in HiFu, laser and aesthetic treatments – also a supplier of professional equipment.
Located in the StorM centre on Ivar Lykkes veg – book via the Timma app for the quickest access to available slots.
Trondheim's artisan bakery Snurr — founded by master pastry chef Lars Lian.
Known for cinnamon buns and fresh bakes. Dining and serving concept in-house.
Danish juice bar and coffee concept known for fast service and energetic atmosphere.
Good for a quick breakfast smoothie or espresso before the workday.
An unpretentious bakery on Brattørkaia, right by the waterfront — perfect for a quick cinnamon bun while watching the Hurtigruten dock.
Brattørkaia is Trondheim's revitalised waterfront, and Easy Bake is a solid stop before catching the fjord ferry.
Bondiskogen is Asker's natural gem — trails around Bondivannet are an everyday walk for Langenga residents.
A short distance from the project. Start at the lower end and walk the lake loop in 30 minutes.
Italian restaurant on Kirkevegen with Neapolitan tradition. Popular for pizza and pasta.
Book a table on weekends — it fills up quickly after 5 PM.
Laid out in English landscape style by brewery owner Erich Christian Dahl and opened to the public in 1883, this Kalvskinnet park is a rare green pocket of old trees and fountains in the city center.
The park sits in front of Trondheims most iconic Art Nouveau building and makes for a perfect pause from the busy city streets.
The Moon Massasje is open six days a week on Fjordgata, Trondheim's most distinctive food street, offering a quiet pause in the middle of the city's busiest commercial corridor.
Located right by the Ravnkloa fish market — combine a seafood visit with an afternoon massage.

Trondheims first modern coffee bar opened by the Old Town Bridge in 1997 and defined the citys coffee culture — the Solsiden outpost carries the legacy forward with hand-brewed coffee across two floors.
Dromedar roasts their own beans and runs their own bakery, so pair your coffee with something fresh from the counter.
Historic park on Stokmovegen. A piece of Stjørdal history in green surroundings.
Nice for a quiet walk with historic charm among old trees.

The name is an old Trondersk expression for having knowledge, and Graffi lives up to it — a casual grill restaurant on Solsiden where a Josper charcoal grill gives everything from steaks to burgers a distinct smoky flavor.
Ask for a table on the terrace facing the canal to pair great grilled food with views of Solsidens waterfront life.
Three minutes' walk from Brøset: a small, intimately run salon where closeness to the client is the business model itself. With a single stylist, personalisation is structural, not a marketing claim.
For residents who want their stylist, not just a stylist: Studio Sax is the neighbourhood's strongest argument for choosing proximity over chain.
The Telegraph is one of Bergen's most distinctive shopping destinations — vintage, design and niche stores.
Good for those shopping outside the mainstream chains. The store mix rotates regularly.
Small park on Strandvegen with a view towards the sea.
Relaxing stop on a walk along Stjørdal's seaside.
Small and charming coffee house in Torgkvartalet. Personal atmosphere and homemade cakes.
A favorite among Torgkvartalet regulars — limited space, but worth the wait.
Floating sauna and cold-water swimming in Laksevåg — fjord proximity and a bracing sauna experience.
Popular for morning bathing. Check seasonal opening and booking options.
Parkering ikea leangen offers shopping in the Ranheim area.
Shopping option in the neighbourhood.
Popular hiking area on the outskirts of Stjørdal with trails and viewpoints.
Bring good shoes — trails range from easy to moderate. Great views over the fjord.
A full-service pharmacy inside City Syd with a broad selection of skincare, supplements and natural remedies – a reliable stop between shops.
Open until 9 PM on weekdays, making it a convenient option for prescription pick-ups after work.
The family restaurant at the heart of City Syd with over 90 dishes, spread across two floors seating 260.
Opens as early as 9 AM on weekdays – a calm oasis for a cup of coffee before the shops fill up.
Specialist clinic for sugar waxing and laser treatments. Over 8 years in Bønes.
Over 400 satisfied customers. Fjellsdalen 1, 8-minute walk.
Bryggeloftet and Bryggestuen is Bergen's most visited restaurant — on Bryggen serving traditional cuisine.
Good for lunch and a taste of Norwegian traditional cooking. Book ahead in tourist season.
Local gym chain with a centre in the neighbourhood.
Standardised equipment and group class offerings.
A neighbourhood pharmacy on Ivar Lykkes veg with personal advice and a broad health selection, away from the shopping centre crowds.
Located near TillerTorget – convenient to combine with a shopping trip without entering the mall itself.
Historic apothecary garden on Nordnes — protected green space with historical character and simple benches.
A good spot for a quiet pause. Rare that such green pockets survive in a dense urban area.
MENY on Hagaløkkveien — well-stocked supermarket with a broad range of fresh produce and fish.
Good parking capacity. Great for weekly shopping and fresh items.
Spa centre with a wide treatment menu — from classic massage to more specialised treatments.
Good at taking new clients and adapting to individual needs.
MENY Solsiden is the nearest full-range supermarket to Nedre Elvehavn, with fresh counters for meat, fish, and cheese, and Norwegian specialties under the Norske Matskatter label.
Open until 10 PM on weekdays — handy for late grocery runs after dinner at Solsiden.
Vitusapotek Solsiden is Trondheim's duty pharmacy, open until midnight every day of the year — with a separate entrance from Innherredsveien when the centre is closed.
The separate entrance is by the corner near Godt Brød — useful to know if you need medicine late at night.
A quiet neighbourhood park near Persaunet with a gentle hill and green lawns — used for sledding in winter and picnics in summer.
Children from Ronningen kindergarten use Elsheimparken as an extension of their playground — a safe and manageable park in the middle of the residential area.
Massage studio in Nøstegaten — relaxing treatments at accessible prices.
Good for a quick recovery after exercise or a long working day.
Budget-friendly gym with long opening hours and free access to equipment and weights.
Low barrier, open late — good for those who want to train without booking classes.
Small artisan bakery in the Frydenlund quarter with fresh bread and a select café menu.
A pleasant lunch stop. Popular with the neighbourhood's workers and stroller crowd.
The unexpected café inside the hardware store – an unpretentious stop for families on a shopping trip.
The kids menu and high chairs make this a practical lunch stop for parents shopping at Biltema.
Mid-Norway's largest fitness chain runs its Moholt location as a self-service facility with a dedicated crosstraining zone — a functional floor that exceeds neighbourhood gym expectations.
Open 05–24 every day: your training schedule runs on your terms, not reception's.
Local hair salon with high customer satisfaction in the Bønes neighbourhood.
One of Bønes' most appreciated salons among residents.
A classic, family-run salon on Granasvegen — the neighbourhood salon in the truest sense, where results and relationships are built over time.
For residents who prefer lasting relationships over anonymous booking apps: here, the stylist remembers you next time.
Recreation area by Havnegata along the sea. Popular for walking and sea air.
Nice for an evening stroll along the water after dinner.
Norway's largest dealer of outdoor hot tubs keeps a showroom on Falkenborgvegen — over 25 years of experience with Arctic Spas and direct imports without middlemen.
Not a spa you visit, but a shop where you test-sit hot tubs for the terrace — surprisingly close for anyone dreaming of outdoor bubbles in the January cold.
Small hair salon in Bønes — personal service in the local area.
A friendly local option for everyday haircuts.
Vitusapotek at Bondi — part of Norway's leading pharmacy chain.
Convenient location between Langenga and the Bondi area.
Massasje Orsagova is tucked away on Vår Frue Strete, a quiet lane in the city centre named after the nearby Church of Our Lady.
A tranquil alternative right in the centre — easy to combine with shopping in Midtbyen.
Plant-based café and juice bar on Adamstuen with a focus on clean ingredients and vegan cuisine.
A firm favourite among health-conscious residents. Strong options for breakfast and lunch.
Trondheimstaket is the city's only public rooftop terrace, atop the newly renovated Nordre gate 12 — Trondheim's first FutureBuilt lighthouse with over 60% circularity index.
Take the panoramic lift from Vaterlandsveita for views of Munkholmen, Nidaros Cathedral, the Fortress and Tyholt Tower — free and open to everyone.
Year-round Oktoberfest vibes on the Solsiden waterfront — Heidis Bier Bar is Trondheims answer to apres-ski culture, with long tables, danceable music and imported German beers.
The place comes alive late at night and on weekends, making it best suited as an energetic finale to a stroll along the wharf.
Agaton Sax — Trondheim-based hairdresser chain, Lade branch.
Multiple branches in Trondheim with the same concept and pricing.
Norway's largest pizza chain with a branch right across the street from the hotel.
Order via the app for faster pickup — perfect for a lazy evening in the hotel room.
TMV-kaia takes its name from Trondhjems mekaniske Værksted, founded in 1872, and is now a vibrant waterfront where industrial heritage meets modern city life.
The area has a playground, restaurants, and outdoor seating — perfect for a break with kids after a stroll along the canal.

With several chefs on the Norwegian Culinary Team since opening in 2003, Broen Bar maintains a remarkably high standard at the waters edge — modern Nordic cuisine built on local ingredients and international inspiration.
The restaurant sits inside Scandic Nidelven with views straight out over the river, so choose a window table for the full experience.
Hair salon focused on natural colour and healthy hair treatments.
Good for those avoiding harsh chemicals. Specialises in vegan hair care.
Student cultural hub since 1951 — concerts, theatre, cinema and debates.
poi_name: Chateau Neuf - The Norwegian Students' Society

value: Cinema Neuf screens arthouse films and student favourites. Open to all, not just students.
poi_name: Chateau Neuf - The Norwegian Students' Society

value: A wellness and spa offering on Starrmyra with services ranging from foot care to tattoos – a broad and unusual spectrum.
Located slightly outside the big shopping centres, in a quieter neighbourhood – call 93 61 42 16 to book.
Park and green space in the neighbourhood — 1355m from the project.
One of the city's green lungs, accessible on foot.
Local market at Stovner Senter with a varied range and affordable prices.
Known for breadth rather than depth — a one-stop shop for various everyday needs.
Norwegian bakery chain with solid bread quality and coffee bar — a reliable morning routine for the neighbourhood.
Opens early. Popular for breakfast shopping and take-away coffee on weekdays.
Extra Grilstad is a large grocery store at Grilstad Marina with a wide product range.
Shopping with a view of the fjord. Good parking facilities.
Troll on Fosenkaia serves Norwegian cuisine with a rebellious twist — cod tongues, grilled halibut, and herb-crusted horse in a set-menu format that defies expectations.
Order the five-course menu for the full experience, and grab a beer on the outdoor terrace overlooking the canal afterward.
Godt Brød is Norway's most recognised organic bakery chain, and the Dronningens gate location is a spacious, modern bake workshop in the heart of Trondheim.
Opens at 6.30 AM on weekdays — ideal for an early breakfast with organic coffee and a cinnamon roll.
Local hair salon in Asker with high customer satisfaction and short waiting times.
Known for personal service and expertise in hair colouring.
Neighborhood store on Værnesgata with a good selection and long opening hours.
Convenient location for evening shopping — open late.
Pharmacy in the neighbourhood with prescriptions, self-care and cosmetics.
Open weekdays and Saturdays. Walk-in for self-care advice.
Charming hotel in Bakklandet's historic wooden house district, right by the Nidelva river and Old Town Bridge.
The airport bus stops at the door. Close to both the office and the city's most photogenic district.
For over thirty years, Den Gode Nabo has served cold drinks and warm food on the banks of the Nidelva — crooked floors and walls in the old warehouse lend an authenticity no new build can match.
The terrace right over the river is one of Bakklandets most coveted outdoor spots, especially on sunny afternoons.

One of Norway's first shopping centres, opened in 1975 — 9,000 square metres covering everything from pharmacy to wine monopoly, hairdresser to chiropractor. Valentinlyst Senter is the neighbourhood's practical hub, not a shopping destination.
The centre consolidates everyday errands in one place — making the week a little more coherent for those who live within walking distance.
International coffee house along Bogstadveien — Oslo's main shopping street west of the centre.
An easy meeting point with good seating. Part of the Bogstadveien routine for many in the area.
National gym chain with this branch well established in Groruddalen.
Wide range of equipment and group classes at competitive prices.

Tucked inside Pirsenteret, where over three thousand people work daily, Pirion Kaffebar is the cafe that fuels Trondheims harbor district — an unpretentious spot surrounded by research and maritime industry.
Pirsenteret itself is worth a look, with its seven interconnected buildings along the harbor — Pirion is the natural stop right in the middle of it all.
Trondheim's own DromedarKaffebar with bakery — a local chain with many locations.
Started in Trondheim; known for in-house roasted coffee and baked goods.
Professional massage studio in Asker centre — a wellness space in everyday life.
Book a massage as a weekly reset. Easy to combine with commuting via Asker station.
Yoga studio in the city centre with a varied class schedule and skilled instructors.
Try a reformer class or vinyasa. Instruction quality is high.
Specialist studio for hot yoga with a fixed sequence of 26 postures in a heated room.
Popular among those committed to the Bikram method. Classes morning and evening.
Actic is one of Asker's most established gyms with a broad class schedule.
Known for reliable equipment and loyal regulars. Good parking.
Pharmacy in Majorstuen with prescriptions, self-care and cosmetics.
Open weekdays and Saturdays. Walk-in for self-care advice.
Snurr's Nyhavna location — artisan bakery in an industrial setting.
Snurr's first non-mall location. Seating and full menu.
Hair salon and beauty centre in Nøstegaten — full service from cuts to treatments.
Good at taking new clients. Reasonable waiting time for an appointment.
Small city park with the pavilion as a gathering point. Used for concerts in summer.
Check the summer program — free concerts and events throughout the season.
SOT grills homemade burgers over charcoal in sourdough buns by the old shipyard — a casual burger bar where the craft matters as much as the atmosphere on Solsidens popular wharf.
The second floor offers better views and a bit more calm than street level, especially on weekends when the waterfront is at its busiest.
Norway's new national museum, opened in 2022 — Europe's largest art museum under one roof.
Munch, Vigeland and Norwegian design history united. The rooftop café overlooks the Oslofjord.
Dedicated yoga and pilates studio from SATS on Majorstuen — all levels welcome.
Timetable ranging from gentle yin classes to dynamic flow. Easy to attend after work.
Banksalen occupies a restored 1882 bank hall seating 200 guests — one of Trondheim's most elegant settings for banquets and dinners.
Ideal for larger events; the exclusive rooms can be privately booked for groups.
Park and green space in the neighbourhood — 1334m from the project.
One of the city's green lungs, accessible on foot.
Joker supermarket in the neighbourhood — groceries and fresh produce.
Open until 10pm on weekdays. The closest stop for everyday shopping.
Hair salon in Stjørdal center.
Book an appointment in advance — drop-in can be difficult on weekends.
Norway's national library, housing one of the world's largest collections of Norwegian culture and knowledge.
Exhibitions open to the public. A cultural landmark on Henrik Ibsens gate.
Renaissance tower from the 1560s at Bergenhus fortress — one of Norway's best-preserved medieval monuments.
Fantastic view from the top. Seasonal opening hours.
Local Deichman branch — a safe learning and meeting place for the whole Romsås neighbourhood.
A popular after-school destination for children and young people in the district.
Large grocery store in Torgkvartalet with a good selection of fresh goods, local products, and ready-made meals.
Two minutes' walk from the hotel — practical for everything from breakfast to evening snacks.
Local museum for Asker's history — cultural heritage from farmsteads to modern urban life.
Especially good for families with children in summer with outdoor activities.
Damsgård is Norway's best-preserved rococo mansion (1770s) — intact interiors and historic park.
Guided tours in the summer season. A unique experience for history enthusiasts.
Right by Trondheim Central Station, Roft Rotisseri serves honest, American-inspired rotisserie and grill food downtown — a no-fuss stop for travelers and locals alike.
The location on Sjogangen makes this a natural choice before or after the train, without compromising on quality.
The budget fitness chain near TillerTorget – in the same building as Jula, with two hours of free parking.
Open 5 AM to midnight every day of the year – perfect for an early morning workout before work.

Asian street food meets Scandinavian design inside the Powerhouse building on Brattorkaia — Kojachi serves a culinary journey through China, Thailand, Korea and Japan in one of Norways most energy-efficient buildings.
The combination of quick Asian fare and the architecturally striking Powerhouse makes this a natural stop along the harbor promenade.

Museumsplass was named in 1909 after the nearby Science Museum, and is today a quiet Kalvskinnet park surrounded by Art Nouveau buildings and monuments — upgraded in 2010 for the museums 250th anniversary.
The park has a playground tucked among the trees and makes a nice alternative to the more central public spaces for a quiet moment.
Authentic Italian restaurant — Da Stefano is a fixed point for Bergen pizza classics.
Good value and affordable. Popular with local families and neighbourhood regulars.
Norway's only nationwide department store chain, with everything from groceries to electronics and building supplies under one roof.
The in-store postal service makes Obs a practical stop for parcel pick-up alongside grocery shopping.
Pharmacy in the neighbourhood with prescriptions, self-care and cosmetics.
Open weekdays and Saturdays. Walk-in for self-care advice.
District shopping centre on Majorstuen with a broad mix of fashion, leisure and daily services.
Underground parking and good public transport. Majorstuen metro station right outside.
The doughnut specialist on Tiller sells two million kroner worth a year from the Kiwi/XXL building – a local favourite.
Located outside City Syd proper, by the Kiwi/XXL building – easy to find for those in the know.
Rosenborg Bakeri has been Trondheims own bakery since 1902, and this Erling Skakkes gate outlet is one of fourteen cozy bakery-cafes spread across the city.
Come early for fresh buns and cinnamon rolls — at a true neighborhood bakery, the best items are the ones straight from the oven.
Neighborhood park on Lade — a green pocket within walking distance.
Benches, open lawn and paths — part of Lade's green fabric.
TrenHer on Fjordgata is a 24-hour gym with modern equipment and spacious facilities, centrally located by the harbour.
329 NOK/month gives access to all seven TrenHer centres in Trondheim — flexible if you're on the move.
A local library in the neighbourhood – a quiet haven for reading, borrowing and digital services amid the commercial district.
Free access to books, newspapers and digital resources – an overlooked amenity for visitors and residents in the Tiller area.
Zumba and dance-fitness studio — specialised in group classes.
poi_name: Baz Berg Activity and Zumbasenter AS

value: Run by a local instructor, focused on dance and rhythm.
