value: Ball court and outdoor activity area at Rommen — a popular gathering spot for young people.
Open space with basketball hoops and tables — an everyday arena for the neighbourhood.
Large open space with grass meadows and nature trails at Tokerud.
Popular for ball games, sledding and dog walking.
Frida on Fjordgata serves authentic Mexican food with ingredients imported directly from Mexico, prepared by Mexican chefs — and the interior was handmade in Mexico and shipped to Norway.
Opens at 2 PM on Saturdays — a good option for an early dinner before a night out.
Martial arts club — kickboxing, boxing and fitness courses.
Active members' club with training for various levels.
A beauty clinic in the Tiller area specialising in skincare and aesthetic treatments.
Book ahead – the clinic has limited capacity and fills up quickly.
SATS gym in the heart of the Bislett quarter — one of the city's most accessible locations.
Large workout floor, equipment for all levels, and classes from early morning.
A calisthenics community based near Clarion Hotel on Brattøra — for those who prefer bodyweight training with a view of the fjord.
The Havnegata area has several outdoor workout parks as well — check along the waterfront promenade.
Small yoga studio at Våkleiven — weekly classes in quiet surroundings.
Run by Vivian Midttveit. Trial class available for newcomers.
Hair salon centrally located in Bønes, 6-minute walk from Våkleivskogen.
Established salon in the area with a broad offering.
Local fast-food joint and pizzeria on Lade — established in 2016.
Pizza, burger, kebab — a casual everyday meal.

Cafe 3B has been an art cafe on Brattorgata since 1985, and in its cellar the Carpe Diem wine bar has opened as a new chapter — wine, photography exhibitions and intimate atmosphere beneath one of Trondheims most iconic venues.
Brattorgata has been called Trondheims coolest street, and 3B is the natural stop for experiencing the streets mix of culture and nightlife.
Bergenhus Fortress is one of Norway's oldest and best-preserved medieval castles, with over 800 years of history.
Free entry to the fortress grounds. Guided tours in season.
SweetGate opened its first Norwegian shop in Trondheim in 2019, with a chocolate and confectionery selection that goes well beyond the ordinary.
Located on Jomfrugata — combine with a stroll through the pedestrian street for the full city centre experience.
With 40 years of experience, Persaunet Hårsenter is the rare example of a salon that has proven its relevance generation after generation — a neighbourhood institution.
A salon you seek out when you want someone who genuinely knows their craft: four decades of experience produce a standard that cannot be bought.
Art café with an organic profile on Søndregata. An alternative meeting place with local art exhibitions.
Calm atmosphere and good coffee — perfect for those who want to avoid the shopping center chaos.
Oasen Yoga offers fitness in the Ranheim area.
Fitness option within walking distance from Overvik.
Dromedar Kaffebar Overvik is Trondheim's first coffee bar, now also in the heart of Overvik. Known for the city's best coffee and freshly baked cakes.
Right in the neighbourhood — Overvik's own coffee bar. Perfect for a quiet start to the day.
Norway's oldest pizza chain since 1970 — Peppes at Leangen delivers the familiar formula with takeaway, delivery, and a wide vegetarian and vegan selection.
Order via Wolt or Foodora to skip the queue on busy Friday evenings — the delivery radius covers the entire Leangen area.
Musikkbiblioteket is NTNU's specialised music library on the third floor of Kjøpmannsgata 42, open to everyone — not just students.
With an NTNU card you have access daily from 7 AM to 11 PM — otherwise it is staffed Monday and Wednesday–Thursday 10 AM–5 PM.
Restaurant by Nordåsvatnet in Straumsgrend — sea views, tapas and Sunday buffet.
110 boat spaces and a floating sauna. An unusual combination of marina atmosphere and good food.
Cosy café and bar in Asker centre — one of the most established local spots.
Great atmosphere on evenings and weekends. Wide selection of drinks and beer.
Bergen's most beloved neighbourhood café — locally roasted coffee and home-baked goods in quiet surroundings.
Quiet and relaxed atmosphere. A good choice for working remotely or a slow meeting.
Clarion Hotel Trondheim commands Brattørkaia with panoramic fjord views — NÒR restaurant and Skybar on the ninth floor are worth a visit whether or not you're staying here.
Take the elevator to the rooftop terrace for a sunset drink — 190 square meters of open views across the fjord and city center.
Kaffemisjonen is one of Norway's most talked-about specialty coffee destinations.
Worth visiting before a walk to Nygårdsparken. Prioritise the pour-over.
Locally known as Lusparken, Brattørparken hides traces of 18th-century merchant gardens behind a busy shortcut between Fjordgata and the Central Station.
Pause next time you rush toward the train — this little garden is surprisingly lush and calm amid the commuter traffic.
Local pharmacy in Vettre — prescriptions and everyday health products within walking distance.
10 minutes' walk from Langenga. Good opening hours and professional service.
Jordbærpikene branch in City Lade — chain focused on juice and ice cream.
A well-known Norwegian concept for fruit drinks and desserts.
One of Trondheim's protected 1933 telephone kiosks, designed by Georg Fredrik Fasting — now converted into a tiny open-air book-lending library in Thornesparken.
Swap a book here on your way through the park — the kiosk is part of a national project filling over a hundred preserved phone booths with free reads.

With roots dating back to the 1700s and named Cafe of the Year by National Geographic in 2012, Baklandet Skydsstation is a time capsule on Bakklandet — homemade food, aquavit and views over the Nidelva toward Nidaros Cathedral.
Ask about the aquavit selection, which includes around 350 varieties — likely the largest collection under one roof in Norway.
Sjogangen spiseri is an ambitious yet unpretentious neighborhood spot on Brattorkaia — Danish-inspired open sandwiches for lunch and seasonal sharing plates for dinner, all built on local produce.
All dishes are designed for sharing, so order broadly and taste your way through the menu together.

Led by Master Dang Thieu Diep, Trondheim Kung Fu Klubb teaches the Kim Son Quang style with a focus on Qi Gong, self-defense and mental training — traditional Chinese martial arts in the heart of Trondheim.
The club welcomes all ages and experience levels, and is an unexpected find along Prinsens gate worth knowing about for active visitors.
E.C. Dahls Bryggeri — Trondheim's historic 1856 brewery with pub and kitchen at Solsiden.
In-house brewery with local beers on tap and traditional Norwegian fare.
A little piece of France at Lade — Franske Nytelser was founded in 2005 by Frenchman Denys Favier, baking croissants and sourdough bread with genuine French craft tradition.
The Campaillou bread has become a local bestseller — a rustic French-inspired sourdough worth a detour.
Retail park with 30 stores spanning sports, children, automotive and personal care — opened in 2007 and expanded with Lade Arena 2 in 2011.
Three hours of free parking across 770 spaces makes Lade Arena a practical stop for larger purchases that are hard to carry home on foot.
USF Verftet is Bergen's most important cultural venue — film, concerts, dance and exhibitions under one roof.
Check the programme at USF.no. From workday to concert evening within walking distance.
An authentic Italian hole-in-the-wall near Persaunet — Il Fornaio bakes pizza in a MAM oven from Modena with ingredients shipped directly from Italy.
The dough follows a ciabatta recipe that yields an airy, crisp crust — a technique rarely found in Norwegian pizzerias.
Var Cafedrom sits right on Kongens gate, the citys central shopping street, offering a relaxed cafe experience in one of Trondheims busiest pedestrian areas.
A solid stop for a quick cup of coffee while in the center — the location in the heart of Midtbyen makes it easy to combine with shopping.
Active since 1995, Trondheim Kickboxing Club is one of the city's oldest martial arts clubs — with a focus on equality and an inclusive environment on the third floor of Dora.
Two weeks of free trial and no prior experience needed — just show up.
Delicatessen and bar in the Nøstet quarter — quality groceries and a well-edited wine list.
Popular stop for take-away deli items and a glass of wine in relaxed surroundings.
The Ranheim Community Museum documents the district's industrial history from the cellulose factory to modern residential district.
Free entry. Interesting for both new and long-time residents of the district.
KIWI supermarket in the neighbourhood — groceries and fresh produce.
Open until 10pm on weekdays. The closest stop for everyday shopping.
Park and green space in the neighbourhood — 833m from the project.
One of the city's green lungs, accessible on foot.
Neighborhood park on Lade — a green pocket within walking distance.
Benches, open lawn and paths — part of Lade's green fabric.
Chopsticks Horizont is a restaurant in the Ranheim area.
Local eatery within walking distance from Overvik.
Local bar on Kjøpmannsgata with an unpretentious atmosphere and reasonable prices.
An authentic local watering hole — this is where you'll meet the regulars.
Jaki Bar by Trondheim Central Station is a pleasant meeting point near the station, with a seasonal a la carte menu and a display case of prepared dishes you can grab and go.
Perfect for a quick, quality meal in connection with a train or bus — the menu surprises with more ambition than the location would suggest.
The Skin Clinic on Jomfrugata is run by surgeon Esther Kuhry, offering injections, laser, and body sculpting performed by doctors and specialist nurses.
All treatments are performed by doctors or specially trained nurses — a clinical tier above most skincare salons in the city.

NTNU University Museum at Kalvskinnet is Trondheims natural and cultural history museum, with exhibitions spanning Norwegian kings and Neanderthals to Arctic wildlife — plus Ringve botanical garden as part of the institution.
The museum sits in a quiet neighborhood with pleasant walking paths and pairs well with a visit to Museumsplass and E.C. Dahls park nearby.
Scandinavian coffee chain — branch at Lade.
Standardised menu with coffee, pastries and lunch.
The outdoor area around Fosslia mountain hall — green and quiet with a playground.
Nice for families with children, with play opportunities in natural surroundings.
Vibeke Glad Hud og Fotterapi offers wellness and treatments.
Local wellness option within walking distance.

Jordbaerpikene has grown into Trondheims own cafe chain with a focus on homemade food and baking — the Solsiden branch sits on the second floor of the center with generous seating and a tempting cake display.
The cafe offers a student discount on food and drinks, making it especially popular among the citys large student population.
Coffee bar connected to Langøra microroastery — Stjørdal's own specialty coffee brand with traceable beans.
Try the seasonal single origin — beans are handpicked and roasted locally at Hjelseng Farm.
The full-range grocer at TillerTorget with fresh counters for meat, fish, cheese and ready meals – Tiller's quality grocery option.
The fresh food section with hand-cut cheese and fresh seafood sets MENY apart from the budget alternatives in the area.
A hair salon chain with drop-in and appointments at TillerTorget – for those who want to combine a haircut with a quick shopping trip.
Open until 8 PM on weekdays and 6 PM on Saturdays, with drop-in availability via the Ledigtime app.
A pharmacy with extended skincare expertise inside TillerTorget – moisture measurement and skin analysis help you find the right product.
Offers flu jabs, travel vaccines and other vaccinations in the pharmacy – order prescriptions online for pick-up within 1 hour.
A shopping centre with 27 shops focused on home and interiors, 9 km south of the city centre – managed by the Olav Thon Group.
Draws around 3,800 visitors on weekdays and 5,000 on Saturdays – over 500 parking spaces available.
The fast-food option inside City Syd – the go-to for teenagers and families in the middle of a long shopping day.
Available via both Wolt and Foodora for delivery, but if you are already inside the mall it is faster to walk in.
Founded in 1858 as the oldest sports association north of Dovre, Trondhjems Turnforening occupies Norways oldest sports building still in use — the 1863 gymnasium on Prinsens gate.
The association offers gymnastics for everyone from age one to a hundred, and the historic premises alone are worth noticing as you walk past.

Built around 1160, the Archbishops Palace is one of Scandinavias oldest secular stone buildings — for centuries the seat of the Archbishop of Nidaros, now home to Norways coronation regalia and three museums.
The courtyard is freely accessible and offers a quiet retreat right next to Nidaros Cathedral, while the museums inside house everything from original sculptures to military history.
Trondheim Flytesenter is an underground retreat on Fjordgata with float tanks, sauna, and massage — a stone's throw from Trondheim Central Station.
Each treatment room is private and includes everything you need — book a couples float for an unconventional city date.
Coop Prix Olderdalen is the local shop for daily groceries. Compact selection, short distance.
Convenient for small shopping — closer than the big stores.
H2 Grilstad Marina is a hairdresser in the neighbourhood.
Local hairdresser within walking distance from Overvik.
Vitusapotek Ranheim covers everyday needs for medicine and health products in the district.
Centrally located at Grilstad Marina. Walking distance from Overvik.
Local shopping centre on St. Hanshaugen with service offerings and grocery stores.
Practical for the neighbourhood — covers most everyday needs without leaving the district.
Extra supermarket in the neighbourhood — groceries and fresh produce.
Open until 10pm on weekdays. The closest stop for everyday shopping.
Fresh pizza in 3 minutes, open 24/7 — Asker's fastest and most flexible pizza stop.
Perfect after a late training session or evening stroll. Automated concept, handcrafted quality.
A retro cafe in the old shipyard building at Solsiden with a 1960s menu, generous outdoor seating and the city's best milkshake.
Shabby chic interiors, local regulars and one of Trondheim's largest terraces right by the river — casual and unpretentious.
Local catering and café with homemade dishes on Stokmovegen.
Good choice for lunch — check the daily menu on social media.

Right on the main square, Trondheim Torg houses around seventy shops and eateries — the facade is covered in mosaics by Roar Wold from 1971, and inside the bronze elephant by Skule Waksvik serves as a local meeting point.
Parts of the center are converted historic wooden houses that have served as shops since the early 1900s — look for them as you walk through.
Hector brings Cali-Mex cuisine to the far end of Solsidens wharf — a colorful, Latin-inspired restaurant where Mexican-Californian fusion meets Trondheim nightlife energy.
Known for its lively atmosphere with Latin music and vibrant decor, the place draws a social crowd especially in the evenings.

A family-run clinic founded by Edel Dah in 1981 and expanded with her daughter Vibeke in 1984, Clinique Cicerone on Kjøpmannsgata blends Eastern acupuncture philosophy with modern skincare in 140 square metres of city-centre spa.
The clinic operates two Trondheim locations — Kjøpmannsgata and Solsiden — making it straightforward to book treatments close to wherever you happen to be.

Britannia Spa, the largest in Trøndelag, occupies the basement of the storied 1870 hotel — originally built for British salmon fishermen — and houses a 1,400 m² wellness facility with a pool, mineral bath, and six treatment rooms.
The spa is complimentary for hotel guests but open to everyone — book treatments in advance to secure a slot.
Sabrura Sticks & Sushi Takeaway Skovgård is a restaurant in the Ranheim area.
Local eatery within walking distance from Overvik.
Lerøy Mat specialises in seafood and western Norwegian delicatessen — fresh fish and everyday food.
A good alternative to the standard grocery run. Fresh fish and local produce.
Affordable department store with everything from snacks to household items on Innherredsvegen.
Useful for stocking up on travel items you might have forgotten.
The southern extension of TillerTorget with XXL, Europris and Power in the adjacent building – a complement to the main centre.
Good access from the E6 motorway and ample parking – practical for bulk shopping without entering the mall.
Archaeological museum beneath Bryggen — artefacts and structures from Bergen after the 1702 city fire.
The foundation of Bryggen's UNESCO status is explained here. Good for all ages.

3T-Solsiden sits inside the Portalen shopping centre in the light-filled corridor between Lilleby and the city centre — a gym that mirrors the neighbourhood itself: relatively new, bright, and oriented towards the fjord.
3T-Klinikken, offering physiotherapy and chiropractic care, shares the same premises — meaning injuries can be assessed and training resumed without ever leaving the building.
Park and green space in the neighbourhood — 1492m from the project.
One of the city's green lungs, accessible on foot.
Central Norway's largest shopping centre with 71 stores and eateries, opened in 1987 and expanded in 2000 – the hub of Tiller's commercial life.
Over 1,000 free parking spaces and a bus stop right outside make the centre easily accessible without a car.
Panipak sits on Nedre Møllenberg — Trondheim's most vibrant neighbourhood street — offering traditional Thai massage with a devoted clientele that rates them 4.9 out of 5.
Book ahead; popular time slots fill up fast, especially on Fridays.

Fire fine sits at the crossroads between Solsiden and Bakklandet, billing itself as Scandinavias freshest club music in premium surroundings — a bar and nightclub with a strong focus on drinks made with natural fruits and juices.
The Verftsgata location places you right between Solsidens restaurant strip and Bakklandets charm, perfect for an evening that starts quiet and ends lively.
Stammen feels more like a living room than a typical city cafe — a cultural venue on Kongens gate serving organic food, vegan buffets and a varied programme of acoustic concerts, comedy and improv.
Check the evening programme before you go — Stammen often hosts events that give the cafe a completely different energy than during the day.
Sporty centre in Fjellsdalen — part of Norway's second-largest gym chain.
Modern equipment and group classes. Fjellsdalen 9, 9-minute walk.
Trondheim's 1910 customs house, designed by Karl Norum, now hosts Bocuse d'Or silver medalist Christopher Davidsen's Nordic gourmet bistro on the Brattøra waterfront.
Book a table in the lounge section if you want to experience the kitchen without committing to a full tasting menu.
Trondheim Maritime Museum occupies a former prison built in 1725, once known as the slave prison, tracing the city's trading and seafaring traditions from the 17th century onward.
The museum oversees the 1866 steam ship SDS Hansteen — check if it is open for tours during the summer season.
Hair salon in Stjørdal center.
Book an appointment in advance — drop-in can be difficult on weekends.
Fitness center on Kjøpmannsgata with a focus on strength and cardio.
Close to the hotel — ask about day passes at the desk.
Trøndelag-based sushi chain with over ten years of experience. Newly opened on Kjøpmannsgata with 4.7 on Google.
Open Thursday to Sunday afternoons — not for weekday lunch, but perfect for weekend indulgence.
Rosenborg Bakeri at Grilstad offers fresh bread and baked goods from the city's famous bakery.
Regular stop for fresh bread. Popular among residents across the district.
Salotto on Nordre gate is run by three stylists with a combined 80 years of experience — a calm salon offering spa scalp massage as an add-on treatment.
Owner Lindis has 40 years of experience — ask for the spa scalp massage add-on for a relaxing experience in the middle of the shopping street.
Trondheim's own bakery since 1902, with 15 outlets across the city – the City Syd branch is the southernmost outpost.
Only the finest ingredients, with no additives across the entire range – a deliberate choice for those who prioritise quality.
Scandinavia's largest hairdressing chain with a salon inside City Syd – free consultation and personalised solutions.
Open until 9 PM on weekdays inside the centre – convenient to book a cut in connection with evening shopping.
Hidden in a Bakklandet courtyard, this playground built entirely from recycled materials was designed by ReMida and Rallar architects and opened in 2018.
Enter from Veita directly across from the bicycle lift — easy to walk past if you don't know it's there.
More than a café — Awake by Trondheim Torg combines specialty coffee with language practice and work inclusion in partnership with the municipality.
A calm alternative to the busy chain cafés downtown, with thoughtful natural-wood interiors and soft lighting.
Fitness center on Stokmovegen with a focus on well-being and holistic training.
Low-threshold and welcoming — good alternative for those who prefer calm training.
Bar and eatery in Nøstegaten — pared-back interior and carefully selected natural wines.
Popular for aperitifs and small plates. Small menu, but thoughtfully curated.
Grilstad Mall gathers shops and services at Grilstad Marina.
Convenient shopping destination with several stores under one roof.
A full-range pharmacy at Rosenborg with good accessibility and professional guidance.
Co-located with Rema 1000 Rosenborg — medication start-up services, inhalation guidance and short wait times make it the neighbourhood's most practical pharmacy.
Craft bakery by day, wood-fired pizzeria by evening — Hevd on the main square leads a double life of sourdough and Italian tradition.
Arrive early for the croissant and sourdough bread selection — the best varieties sell out fast.
Trondheim's largest shopping centre on Lade — over 90 shops and eateries.
Groceries, fashion and services under one roof, within walking distance of home.
Trøndelag County Library shares premises with Trondheim Public Library at Peter Egges plass, named after the Trønder author when the new building opened in 1988.
The collections are shared and open to everyone — the fourth floor offers quiet reading room seats overlooking the city's cultural quarter.
Artisan bakery in Strandgaten with a focus on long fermentation and sourdough.
Bread sells out early at weekends. Pick something up on your Saturday shopping run.
Vitusapotek inside Sirkus Shopping — wide selection and pharmacy advice within walking distance of Leangen.
Ten minutes walk. Practical to combine with grocery shopping at Coop Mega in the same mall.
Traditional Thai massage near Sirkus Shopping — relaxation and wellness in the neighborhood.
Ten minutes walk from Leangen. Popular with locals for stiff shoulders after office hours.
At the tip of the pier named after Norway's eternal king, with sweeping views across the Trondheim Fjord and the transformed waterfront.
One of the city's best sunset spots — bring coffee and find a west-facing bench.
Frisør Velde has been on Innherredsveien since 1993 — a veteran among the city's salons, with owner Mona Velde behind the scissors for over three decades.
Student cuts at 299 NOK make this one of the most affordable quality options near the centre — right by Nedre Elvehavn.
Italian pizza craft in two formats — classic round tradizionale for one, or a half-metre Roman pala for sharing, right by Trondheim Central Station.
Best suited as a quick stop — grab-and-go works just as well as dining in.
Simens Isbar is Norway's ice cream champion and Trondheim's most popular dessert spot — homemade gelato, Belgian waffles, and milkshakes along the Brattøra promenade.
Take your ice cream out to the pier or the skatepark bench — Simen himself is often behind the counter.
Music café and book bar in one on Nedre Bakklandet, where live concerts, candlelight and wall-to-wall bookshelves create an atmosphere that is hard to leave.
Walk all the way to the book bar at the back — from there you have views of the river, the city bridge and Nidaros Cathedral.
A popular Thai kitchen with a weekday lunch buffet that draws office workers from across the Tiller area.
The lunch buffet runs from noon to 3:30 PM on weekdays – arrive early for the best selection of spring rolls and fried noodles.
H2 Frisør is a hairdresser in the neighbourhood.
Local hairdresser within walking distance from Overvik.
An established salon with fourteen staff and a branch inside Sirkus Shopping — known for Joico products and online booking that makes scheduling effortless.
Easy to combine a cut with other errands at the centre — they keep hours that match Sirkus Shopping's long evening schedule.
Norwegian bakery chain with a local Trondheim branch.
Fresh bread and pastries from their own bakeries across the country.
H2 salon at City Lade — a Nordic chain with locations across Trondheim.
Easy access from the same mall as the City Lade shops.
Apotek 1 Elefanten — one of Norway's largest pharmacy chains, Lade branch.
Located centrally in the City Lade area with easy parking and transit.
Obs! City Lade — hypermarket covering groceries, home and leisure.
One of Coop's largest stores in the region, co-located with City Lade.
Trondheim's HYROX gym and home for functional fitness since 2007, with a training philosophy that suits all levels.
Structured group classes offer more intensity than open gym — ideal for those who thrive on community-driven workouts.
Historic bobsleigh track — a unique feature in the local forest landscape.
An unusual local attraction with historical significance for the district.
Apotek 1 inside Xhibition shopping centre — accessible during your shopping trip.
Good for collecting prescriptions during a shopping visit. Good opening hours.
Xhibition is Bergen's second-largest shopping centre — 80+ stores and food services in the centre.
Easy to reach on foot from Nøstebukten. Comprehensive offering for everyday shopping.
Now known as Evolve Academy, this Dora venue unites MMA, BJJ, boxing, and Muay Thai under one roof — Trondheim's most complete combat sports centre.
Båtsmannsgata 4 houses several martial arts clubs in the same building — you can try multiple disciplines without changing address.
Trondheim's first coffee bar — Dromedar on Nordre gate set the standard for specialty coffee in the city and still holds it.
Freshly baked cakes from their own bakery are just as much a reason to visit as the coffee.
French bakery atmosphere on Ullevålsveien with croissants, open sandwiches and pâtisserie.
Expect queues on Saturday mornings. Visit on a weekday morning for the quietest experience.
A hair and wellness centre with ten staff at City Syd – eight hairdressers and two skin and foot therapists under one roof.
Bus 46 from Trondheim centre stops right behind the building – book via the Fixit app to secure an appointment.
Authentic Thai in a cozy alley in the city centre since 2012 — Benja Siam in Ravelsveita is one of the city's best-kept secrets.
Easy to walk past in the narrow alley — follow the sign in from the street, it's worth the detour.

Set inside the 1660s walls of Kristiansten Fortress, Restaurant Kommandanten serves food made from scratch using Trøndelag producers — where the city's military history becomes the backdrop for one of the centre's most distinctive outdoor dining terraces.
The restaurant and its protected fortress rooms are available for private events — worth keeping in mind for memorable dinners overlooking the city.
Norway's oldest scientific library, founded in 1768 and named after Bishop Gunnerus, with collections stretching back to the 1500s.
Open to the public — a quiet refuge at Kalvskinnet with an atmosphere few modern libraries can match.
Spesial serves classic Norwegian food in pleasant surroundings — soup, open sandwiches and a daily special.
Solid lunch option within walking distance. Simple and good without trying too hard.
Gym with personal follow-up and a welcoming local community.
A good alternative to the big chains. Less queuing and more attention per trainer.
24/7 accessible gym at Haugenstua with a fully equipped training floor.
Affordable monthly fee with key card access — open even in the middle of the night.
Football pub on Lademoen — local MonkeyBrew on tap.
Casual sports bar with multiple screens and a broad beer selection.
Nong Song Thai Massage sits at Nedre Møllenberg gate 94, in the heart of Trondheim's densest cluster of Thai massage salons.
Easy walk-in option for those who don't plan far ahead.
Trondheim's most popular gym chain with a large training area at Leangen — weights, group classes and swimming pool.
Under eight minutes walk. Pool, sauna and hot tub make this more than just a gym.
Casual pinsa and sandwich bar on Solsiden's restaurant strip, where the marina and outdoor seating set the mood.
Works best as a quick, uncomplicated stop between Solsiden's more ambitious restaurants.
Asker's local donut bakery — fresh donuts in every flavour.
Popular treat destination for Friday sweets. Order online or pop in.
Central Norway's leading budget fitness chain, with FITcert Level 4 certification – the highest European standard.
Open 5 AM to midnight year-round from 299 kr/month with no commitment, Impulse Online app included in the membership.
Award-winning riverside architecture with a glass-roofed atrium. 336 rooms and conference facilities in the heart of the city.
poi_name: Radisson Blu Royal Garden Hotel, Trondheim

value: The 26 North restaurant serves Nordic cuisine. Central for guests visiting the office.

value: Specialized training center for powerlifting and performance-based training — three minutes from Leangen.
Right next to the new district. A niche environment for those who take training seriously.
Local café and eatery at Vestli — homely atmosphere with simple food.
A well-known meeting place for Vestli residents, 10 minutes' walk from Stovner Torg.
Dromedar Kaffebar on Bakklandet is Trondheim's most iconic café — right opposite the Old Town Bridge, with house-roasted coffee and 28 years of local coffee culture behind it.
Sit outside with the view toward the Old Town Bridge and the wharves — the best coffee experience in Trondheim.
Cowboys and Angels on Solsiden is a Spanish-inspired barbershop with classic interiors, straight razor shaves, and skin fades right on the Nidelva waterfront.
Book online or drop in — rated 4.7 out of 5, this is Solsiden's most popular barbershop.
Small neighborhood park in a quiet residential area along Husbyvegen.
A quiet green lung slightly away from the city center noise.
Family restaurant with an extensive menu and child-friendly atmosphere. Norwegian restaurant chain.
Popular for weekend brunch and family lunch — kids eat free on many occasions.
The national museum for police, judiciary and correctional services, housed in a building that served as a penal labour facility from 1833 and Norway's first criminal asylum from 1895.
Two buildings to explore — the old criminal asylum and the military hospital offer a rare window into Norwegian legal history.
Outdoor fitness park in the Marka forest — climbing walls, weight benches and cardio stations.
Free and open around the clock. Combine the workout with a hike in Gjelleråsmarka.
Local pizza and grill restaurant on Søndregata with high ratings. A regular stop for Stjørdal's youth.
Large pizza at a good price — call and order for quick pickup.
Oslo's own specialty coffee chain, founded on Grünerløkka in 1994. Grinds and brews coffee daily.
Loyal regulars in Frogner. Good coffee at a fair price — not a Starbucks clone.
Italian, Turkish and Mexican cuisine under one roof at Stovner Senter — the district's popular restaurant meeting point.
Direct entrance from outside — no need to go through the shopping centre.
The harbour promenade stretches from Skansen to Brattøra with benches, sculptures and views across the fjord to Munkholmen — Trondheim's finest waterfront walk.
The promenade is set up for swimming in summer — bring a towel and jump in from the pier on a warm day.

A craft bakery rooted in Tyholt, where everything is baked from scratch using only genuine ingredients — no shortcuts, no compromise. After 16 years under the same ownership, Mikalsen has become the neighbourhood's quiet institution for things that taste right.
Picking up your Saturday bread here isn't about trends — it's about knowing your part of the city.
Habitat is Trondheim's answer to the perfect craft bar: 24 taps, sourdough pizza, and their own microbrewery, Monkey Brew, in the cellar — rated Norway's best on Untappd.
Ask the bartender about the daily experimental brew from Monkey Brew — there's always something new.
H2 Barber Mercur operates inside the historic Mercurgården, combining Norwegian hairdressing craft with barbershop culture in one of the city's finest buildings.
Rated 4.9 out of 5 from over 300 reviews — book well ahead, this is the city's most sought-after barbershop.
Mercurgården dates to 1863 and has housed a stock exchange, post office, and telegraph station — today Illums Bolighus at street level is a must for Scandinavian design lovers.
Look for the Mercury statues both inside and out — the building won Trondheim's real estate prize in 2022 after a careful restoration.
Contemporary art gallery on Majorstuen with changing exhibitions by Norwegian and international artists.
Free entry. One of the more respected smaller galleries in the city's western art scene.
Trondheim Public Library Ranheim is the district's library branch with activities for children and adults.
Free meeting place with children's section and events. Walking distance from Overvik.
A local bakery café in the quiet surroundings of Svartholtet, away from the shopping centre bustle – a moment of calm with coffee and homemade pastries.
Open weekdays only until 4:30 PM, so this is a place you plan to visit, not one you stumble upon.
A smaller shopping centre between TillerTorget and City Syd with Jernia and specialist shops – heated underground parking with 3 hours free.
The focus on home and interiors makes StorM a complement rather than a competitor to the larger centres.
A specialist in hair extensions and hair care in the Tiller area – a niche offering for those seeking more than a standard cut.
Call 920 33 888 to book – a specialised salon focused on extensions and hair quality.
Hair salon in Stjørdal center.
Book an appointment in advance — drop-in can be difficult on weekends.
Hair salon in Stjørdal center.
Book an appointment in advance — drop-in can be difficult on weekends.
3T is Trøndelag's largest gym chain. Modern center with everything from weights to group classes.
Day passes available at reception — well equipped with locker rooms and sauna.
Dype Roetter - Kafe Spire is a café in the Ranheim area.
A pleasant stop for coffee and a bite to eat.
Twelve self-guided, motorised training machines that deliver a complete 40-minute session without requiring a single active decision from you. The antithesis of the traditional gym floor.
Ideal for residents at any life stage: the system scales automatically, and you need neither a plan nor prior experience to get started.
Extra grocery store at Stovner Senter — budget-friendly with a decent range for everyday shopping.
Handy for quick purchases near Stovner Torg.
Walk-in hairdresser with no appointment needed — convenient for a quick trim.
Fast throughput and affordable pricing. Popular among young people and busy families.
Neighbourhood café at Stovner Senter with simple food and a relaxed atmosphere.
A gathering spot for the district — simple lunch and coffee without fuss.
Sushi and wok dishes at Stovner Senter — the only sushi restaurant in the district.
Wide selection of rolls and wok dishes for lunch and dinner.
Asian-inspired tea bar at Trondheim Torg with organic tea, real fruit chunks and plant milk — no manufactured syrups.
Everything is blended fresh on-site, and all teas can be customized with vegan alternatives.
Neighbourhood café — coffee, cakes and light lunch.
A gathering spot for locals within walking distance of home.
Brilliance cleaning is a restaurant in the Ranheim area.
Local eatery within walking distance from Overvik.
One of Trondheim's most accessible fitness centres, tucked into the base of Valentinlyst shopping centre with free parking and equipment covering everything from heavy lifting to group classes.
The neighbourhood's no-fuss gym: no planning required, you just go.
An intimate skincare salon on Dronningens gate with treatments for everyone — from waxing to facials.
Run by Charlotte Severinsen since 2010 — a small, personal salon where you quickly become a regular.
One of Troendelag's largest shopping centers with around 100 stores — opened in 2012 at Strindheim, just 330 metres from Leangen station.
The airport bus stops right outside — four stops with over 1,450 daily departures make Sirkus a natural hub for the entire eastern city.
Frisør Orkide in Taraldsgårdsveita offers threading — an ancient Eastern hair-removal technique using thread that is gentle on the skin.
The veita is one of Trondheim's charming narrow lanes in the old town — the salon is tucked away but worth finding for precision thread work.
Small pocket park in the new residential area along Meierivegen.
A modern addition to urban development — benches and greenery for a short break.
Extra supermarket in the neighbourhood — groceries and fresh produce.
Open until 10pm on weekdays. The closest stop for everyday shopping.
Kunsthall Trondheim opened in 2016 in the city's former fire station and is now Trøndelag's largest arena for contemporary art, with free admission.
Beyond exhibitions, the programme offers concerts, performances, film screenings and talks — check the weekly schedule before dropping in.
A literature house cafe with barista-championship pedigree, where the seasonal menu shifts and the books never run out.
Named after Hamsun's novel character and housed in the old fire station — Trondheim's most literary address for coffee and evening drinks.
Norway's coronation regalia — royal crowns and robes used since King Charles John's coronation in 1818 — displayed in the west wing of the medieval Archbishop's Palace.
One of the city's more compact museum exhibitions, but the historical weight of the objects more than makes up for it.
Local hair salon in the centre — skilled service and a personal approach.
Takes new clients. Suitable for all hair types and needs.
Piraten frisør is based in Pirsenteret by the harbour — a barbershop with a maritime name and location right next to Trondheim's historic wharf district.
Pirsenteret also has a REMA 1000 and cafés, so combine your haircut with a quick grocery run or coffee with fjord views.
Japanese and Burmese cuisine combined — a rare pairing and well executed.
Popular for take-away and table reservations. Good sushi quality at reasonable prices.
The world's best-preserved medieval leprosarium — 600 years of Bergen's medical history intact.
A moving and well-told exhibition. Rarely preserved authenticity.
Specialty coffee roasted in Trøndelag — light-roasted, precision-brewed and served in the Architects' House.
Started in a six-square-metre room behind a hair salon in 2012, survived bankruptcy and re-emerged as the city's most uncompromising coffee bar.
Extra supermarket in the neighbourhood — groceries and fresh produce.
Open until 10pm on weekdays. The closest stop for everyday shopping.
Hair salon in Stjørdal center.
Book an appointment in advance — drop-in can be difficult on weekends.
Italian restaurant and pizzeria on Kjøpmannsgata with a classic menu.
Family-friendly with good pizzas — popular among local families with children.
A full-service pharmacy in Strindheim — the closest option when everyday life demands it.
Conveniently located in Strindheim centre. Solves what it needs to solve.
Casual bar and restaurant on TMV-kaia where charcoal-grilled burgers, tacos and weekend DJs set an inclusive, laid-back tone at Solsiden.
Weekend evenings feature DJs and dancing between the tables — a perfect transition from dinner to night out without changing venue.
Kafé Skuret occupies an old boat shed on Fosenkaia — a charming concert venue with Trondheim's cheapest beer, homemade waffles, and views of wooden boats in the canal.
Come on Sunday for coffee and fresh waffles after a stroll along the Nidelva river.
The original outlet of G. Johnsen, Stjørdal's oldest bakery. Everything baked from scratch, every day.
Perfect for a quick breakfast bite — grab coffee and fresh rolls for your walk.
Central Norway's largest and oldest yoga centre has been based on Bakklandet since the early 1990s, offering everything from vinyasa to yin in bright, welcoming studios.
Combine with a walk along the Nidelva after class — Bakklandet is Trondheim's most beautiful neighbourhood.

Middelhavets Marked on Dronningens gate is Trondheim's most sought-after specialty shop for Mediterranean food — with fresh produce, Turkish brands, and spices you won't find in regular Norwegian stores.
Ask the staff for spice and pulse recommendations — they know their stock inside out.
Impulse gym is located inside Pirbadet — Norway's largest indoor water park — with views over the Trondheim Fjord and Munkholmen from the training floor.
Combine your workout with the swimming hall in the same building, and take bus 21 or 28 which stop right outside.
Hairdresser in the immediate neighbourhood — known for quality craft and personal service.
Visit early in the week for shorter waiting times. Popular among local residents.
SATS gym with well-equipped training floor and a wide class schedule in Laksevåg.
Easy day pass option. Good class capacity outside rush hours.
Starbucks on Kongens gate sits in the middle of Trondheim's pedestrian street, with outdoor seating and wifi access — a familiar anchor for travellers.
A solid starting point for exploring Midtbyen on foot — Nidaros Cathedral is a ten-minute walk away.
Bølgelengde is an established hair salon in the local area with a loyal clientele.
Easy to book an appointment. Good reputation for cuts and treatments.
Maritime museum focusing on Bergen's role as a seafaring city — ship models, navigation and harbour history.
Good museum for children and maritime enthusiasts. Rich collection spanning many eras.
Dokkparken sits alongside Dokkhuset Scene, a concert venue founded in 2006 by four music organisations that make Nedre Elvehavn a living cultural quarter.
Check Dokkhuset's programme for chamber music and jazz — the 220-seat hall offers an intimate concert experience right by the water.
Thon Senter Bergen is one of Bergen's larger shopping centres — full coverage of chain stores and grocery shops.
Good for a combined shopping errand. Parking available in the basement.
Espresso House at Asker station — the commuter's regular morning stop.
Opens early and gets you ready for the train. Always a short queue in rush hour.
Yogaskolen offers instruction in classical yoga and meditation — thorough and unhurried approach.
Suitable for all levels. Regular courses and drop-in classes available.
Named in 1982 to honour Norwegian war sailors, Krigsseilerplassen holds a 1981 bronze sculpture by Kristofer Leirdal commemorating seafarers lost in both World Wars.
The square sits right between the Maritime Museum and Radisson Blu Royal Garden — a quiet, historic pocket in the harbour district.
A gym in the heart of Midtbyen focused on smart training — centrally located on Nordre gate for those who want to squeeze in a session between city errands.
The central location makes it a convenient option for a quick workout right in the middle of town.
Popular recreation area with sledding hill and viewpoint between Persaunet and Tyholt.
The neighborhood's natural gathering place — sledding in winter, picnics and play in summer.
Fitness studio aimed at women — dance and group classes.
Studio concept inside the City Lade building.
Thai massage centrally in Stjørdal. Traditional treatments for relaxation and well-being.
Book in advance — slots fill up quickly, especially on weekends.
Well-established Chinese restaurant centrally on Kjøpmannsgata. Popular for takeaway and family dinners.
Large selection of dishes at reasonable prices — good for an informal dinner with kids.
Coop Prix supermarket in the neighbourhood — groceries and fresh produce.
Open until 10pm on weekdays. The closest stop for everyday shopping.
A barbershop on Prinsens gate where regulars pass other salons just to get here.
One of the city's highest-rated men's barbers — informal, affordable and with loyal customers who never switch.
Highly rated halal takeaway, conveniently located near Stovner T-bane.
Ideal for an evening takeaway after work or the gym.
Niche shopping centre in the Majorstuen quarter with selected retailers and specialist shops.
Less commercial than Colosseum Center — good for more curated purchases.
A Bergen bakery institution since 1864 — celebrated for skoleboller and everyday bread across the city.
Neighbourhood bakery for regulars. The school bun day is Friday.
Creative sushi takeaway at Solsiden with unexpected flavours like strawberry passionfruit and tempura rolls.
Perfect for a quick, well-composed lunch between the Nidelva and Solsiden Senter — no need to sit down.
Impulse Grilstad offers group classes and strength training at Grilstad Marina.
Alternative to 3T for those who prefer a smaller centre.
Showroom for hot tubs, saunas and spa equipment — Polarbad is central Norway's largest specialty store for home wellness.
Six minutes walk. Test saunas and hot tubs on-site before you invest.
Robata Asian Fusion pairs sushi, dim sum, and charcoal-grilled meats on Munkegata — one of Trondheim's longest-running addresses for Asian fusion.
Request a window table for views down Munkegata towards the fjord.
A former military magazine from 1880, named after historian P.F. Suhm, now housing the Science Museum's medieval exhibition — nominated for European Museum of the Year.
The medieval exhibition provides a surprisingly deep look into Trondheim's oldest history in a compact, accessible format.
Hair salon in Stjørdal center.
Book an appointment in advance — drop-in can be difficult on weekends.
Bassengbakken park is a modern urban park at Nedre Elvehavn, named after the slope down to Rosenborgbassenget, with generous seating along the canal.
Nearby Trenerys gate is named after British engineer John Trenery, the first director of Fabriken ved Nidelven — industrial history written into the street names.
The student café in Gunnerusbygget at Kalvskinnet, with a hot food buffet paid by weight — everyday, affordable and right in the campus environment.
Open to everyone, not just students — one of the most budget-friendly lunch spots in the city centre.
Neighborhood park on Lade — a green pocket within walking distance.
Benches, open lawn and paths — part of Lade's green fabric.
Rosenborg Bakeri — Trondheim-based chain with pastries in the neighbourhood.
The bakery supplies several branches across the city.
Impulse Treningssenter offers fitness in the Ranheim area.
Fitness option within walking distance from Overvik.
Expert patisserie — professional confectionery technique and seasonal cakes in a central setting.
A solid choice for dessert or afternoon coffee near Bryggen.
Small yoga studio on Majorstuen with personal guidance and varied yoga styles.
Intimate atmosphere — good for beginners and those who prefer smaller classes.
Restaurant and bar on Kjøpmannsgata with a varied menu and central location.
Flexible spot for everything from lunch to evening food with friends.
Kaffebrenneriet in Asker centre — well-known Norwegian coffee chain with consistent quality.
Always freshly roasted coffee and comfortable seating. Convenient by the Trekanten entrance.
Public dog park — accessible year-round.
Popular with dog owners from across eastern Trondheim.
Local hairdresser by Bislett with engaged stylists and a good neighbourhood feel.
Affordable and friendly. Familiar faces among the regulars in Bislett's daily life.
The neighborhood's top-rated hair salon — personal service and a short walk from Leangen.
Seven minutes walk. Book ahead, the salons at Leangen are popular.
Transit on Fjordgata is Trondheim's largest second-hand store and coffee bar in one — vintage clothes, retro furniture, and barista coffee, where you can buy the chair you're sitting on.
Set aside at least half an hour — it's easy to lose track of time among art, antiques, and good coffee.
French bakery and delicatessen in central Bergen — long baguettes and homemade preserves.
Good spot for breakfast shopping. Order croissant and coffee at the counter.
Norway's largest Holdbart store — 2,600 sqm selling food that would otherwise go to waste.
Opened in 2020. Bulk buys at reduced prices of goods that cannot be sold in regular stores.
Cinemateket in Olavshallen screens film history and arthouse rarities — with a 35mm projector for analogue prints and tickets at just 50 NOK.
The entrance is from the corner of Olav Tryggvasons gate and Krambugata at street level — easy to walk past if you don't know it's there.
Bobby's Bar sits in the middle of Trondheim's restaurant strip and is one of the city's most popular nightlife spots — eclectic vibe, solid cocktails, and frequent live music on Carl Johans gate.
Opens as early as 3 PM — perfect for an early Friday pint on the restaurant strip.
Bar in the Bryggen district — intimate setting with a considered selection of spirits and cocktails.
One of Bergen's more refined bar experiences. Book ahead at weekends.
Indoor football cage on Lade — rent a pitch for small-sided games.
Specialised concept for short-pitch play year-round indoors.
France's cultural embassy in Oslo with concerts, films, exhibitions and language courses.
Monthly programme always includes a surprising element — check the website regularly.
Trondheim's own bakery since 1902 — Rosenborg Bakeri was started by master baker Magnus Helgesen and is now run by the fourth generation with over 600 products.
The City Lade branch is closest to Leangen — a perfect stop for fresh rolls and coffee on the way to work.
Rock, metal and punk in a cavern-like basement on Kjøpmannsgata — Fru Lundgreen is Trondheim's fearless venue for live music and concerts.
Check the concert schedule before heading out — the best evenings are when there's a live band on stage.
Jakobsli Hårstudio avd. Ranheim is a hairdresser in the neighbourhood.
Local hairdresser within walking distance from Overvik.
Barbershop at Stovner Senter offering traditional shaving and modern haircuts.
Well known in the district for good service and reasonable prices.
Jan Schanke has been cutting Trondheim's hair for generations from Kjøpmannsgata — now part of the Apollo network as Norway's leading hair and scalp specialist.
For anyone needing specialist help with hair loss or scalp issues, this is the place — with over 30 years of expertise in the field.
Defence museum within the fortress complex — documents Bergen's coastal and city defence through history.
Free entry. Great for history enthusiasts already visiting the fortress grounds.
A memorial to Holocaust survivor Julius Paltiel, unveiled on International Holocaust Day in 2015, featuring a colourful round table symbolizing equality and inclusion.
The round table is illuminated in the evenings and serves as a quiet, reflective gathering point where Erling Skakkes gate meets Elvegata.
Summer favourite by the fjord in Leangbukta — Mediterranean food with boat mooring.
Open spring to autumn. Book a table on the terrace for views over the bay.
Asian-inspired with a Norwegian twist at Solsiden — Sabrura serves sushi, sticks and dim sum in a relaxed setting by the marina.
The all-you-can-eat buffet is popular and fills up quickly — arrive early for the best selection.
Donut specialist on Lade — doughnuts and coffee.
Straightforward take-away concept focused on doughnuts.
A shopping centre in the old shipyard brick building with 53 stores, a spa and views over the mouth of the Nidelva.
Concert stage in summer, ice rink in winter — Solsiden is more neighbourhood living room than shopping street.
Rosenborg Bakeri at Solsiden is a branch of Trondheim's own bakery since 1902 — now run by the fourth-generation Helgesen family, with over 600 products in the range.
Try the skolebolle and coffee for a classic Trondheim bakery experience.
Good Omens is Fjordgata's rock and metal bar with a compact stage, board games, retro consoles, and affordable microbrews — a laid-back refuge by the harbor.
Bring friends for quiz night or karaoke — prices are among the lowest in the city center.
Bergen Public Library — the city's largest public library with a wide offering for all age groups.
Free entry and free lending. Study spaces, events and digital services.
Nordnes Park is the green lung of the peninsula — paths, benches and panoramic views over the fjord.
Established in 1888 and still Bergen's finest neighbourhood park. Nordnes Sjøbad lies within it.
Feel24 Langenga — 24/7 modern gym in the Askerhallen complex, 4 minutes from Langenga.
Always open. Flexible monthly membership and broad equipment range for all levels.
MT Byggteknikk is a green area in the district.
Great for walks and relaxation in the neighbourhood.
Pharmacy in Majorstuen with prescriptions, self-care and cosmetics.
Open weekdays and Saturdays. Walk-in for self-care advice.
Byhaven opened in 1999 with 32 shops across four floors on Olav Tryggvasons gate, topped by apartments that became Trondheim's first rooftop-living project.
The Vinmonopolet in the lower level is the most centrally located in the city — perfect for picking up a bottle on the way back to the hotel.
Norway's oldest pizza chain since 1970 — Peppes at Leangen delivers the familiar formula with takeaway, delivery, and a wide vegetarian and vegan selection.
Order via Wolt or Foodora to skip the queue on busy Friday evenings — the delivery radius covers the entire Leangen area.
Norway's first sports club for pole — POA is based in the Pirbadet building at the harbour with bright, modern facilities and classes for all levels.
Enter through Pirbadet's reception and up the stairs — don't let the route confuse you the first time.
A new performance centre on Travbaneveien dedicated to functional training and HYROX — founded by four fitness devotees who spent four years scouting the right space.
Just a three-minute walk from Spiltauet — the closest gym for residents, with an indoor artificial turf pitch and varied group classes.
Thai food at Stovner Senter — fresh flavours and quick service on weekdays.
Popular for lunch and takeaway among workers in the area.
Hair salon in Stjørdal center.
Book an appointment in advance — drop-in can be difficult on weekends.
A neighbourhood salon with roots stretching back to 1984 — one of Leangen's most established hairdressers, run by Audhild Tystad with six permanent staff on Falkenborgvegen.
A perfect recommendation rate from every customer, and you book by phone — the kind of place where the regulars are greeted by name.
Unique museum of children's art from over 180 countries — a centre for creativity and diversity.

value: Especially popular with families with children. Free entry for children under 3.

value: Massage and acupuncture in the centre — traditional treatments with experience.
Good at combining massage and acupuncture in the same visit.
Piraten frisør AS is a hairdresser in the neighbourhood.
Local hairdresser within walking distance from Overvik.
Fully renovated in 2022, Marinen trim park sits along the Nidelva river near Nidaros Cathedral with a bouldering stone, exercise equipment and the city centre's largest playground.
Combine a workout with a walk along the riverbank — the equipment has guidance signs for both beginners and advanced users.
Labour museum near Youngstorget, covering Norway's trade union history and workers' struggles.
A little-known hidden gem in the centre. Free entry.
A gourmet restaurant at Radisson Blu Royal Garden celebrating Trøndelag's produce with seasonal menus and an international touch.
The seasonal menus change regularly — ask for the day's recommendation to get the best of the local produce.
IKEA Restaurant - Leangen is a restaurant in the Ranheim area.
Local eatery within walking distance from Overvik.
Pharmacy at Vestli T-bane — a convenient collection stop on the way home.
High user rating among Vestli residents. Known for quick service.
Snurr Craft Bakery occupies Sommergården, one of Trondheim's most recognisable buildings on the corner of Kongens gate at the main square.
Everything is baked with natural ingredients and no shortcuts — the sourdough is worth the detour.
Kråka Pub serves hand-crafted beer from the local Wettre Brewery on the Søndre Vettre farm.
Open Thu–Sat. Book a beer tasting for friends or colleagues — Asker's best microbrewery.
Large SATS centre by Colosseum Park with an extensive class range and parking available.
Practical if you combine a workout with shopping at Colosseum Center.
The Norwegian Combat Academy offers fitness in the Ranheim area.
Fitness option within walking distance from Overvik.
Classic Oslo cinema in the centre with broad programming and good atmosphere.
One of the city's older cinema venues — good for film nights with a different feel from a multiplex.
Oslo cinema with a good auditorium and a broad selection of current films.
Part of the Nordisk Film Kino chain. Easy access from Rådhusplassen and the city centre.
Bib Gourmand-awarded neighbourhood restaurant on Ullevålsveien with sharing plates, natural wine and a regular-crowd feel.
Opened in 2012. The daily special at 4–6pm is the neighbourhood's best value for money.
French comfort food made with first-class local produce, right on Munkegata — Le Bistro is Trondheim's answer to the Parisian neighbourhood bistro.
The wine list has a strong selection from Burgundy — ask for a pairing recommendation for the full experience.
Nordic coffee house focused on single-origin coffee and hand-brewed tea in calm surroundings.
poi_name: Little Valkyrie Coffee and Tea House

value: A quiet alternative to the larger chains — good as a work café in the mornings.
poi_name: Little Valkyrie Coffee and Tea House

value: Handcrafted bagels in one of Trondheim's most charming neighbourhoods — Nabolaget Bagelri sits among the wooden houses of Nedre Bakklandet and has quickly become a local favourite.
Open Tuesday to Saturday, closed Mondays — arrive early on Saturdays, they often sell out.
Hair salon in Stjørdal center.
Book an appointment in advance — drop-in can be difficult on weekends.
Multicultural hair salon with broad expertise in African and curly hair types.
Specialist knowledge that is hard to find elsewhere in Bergen.
A viewpoint on the pedestrian bridge over the Nidelva river at Klostergata, with panoramic views of the river bend and the old wooden houses along the banks.
Stop in the middle of the bridge — from here you can see the river, Øya and the cathedral spire all in one glance.
Classic café near the National Theatre with traditional Norwegian dishes and open sandwiches.
A calm alternative to the city centre rush. Popular with regulars from the theatre and arts scene.
The Solsiden skating rink sits in the middle of a former shipyard, with over 3,000 metres of cooling loops beneath the ice and heat-recovery technology from KLP.
Open from November to Easter — arrive early on weekdays to skip the queue, as the rink is hugely popular with locals.
Botanical garden at Ringve — open parkland with curated collections.
NTNU-run garden with themed sections and collections from around the world.
Pizzabakeren is Asker's local pizza chain — a reliable choice for family evenings.
Central location near Asker station, takeaway and delivery available.

Impulse Solsiden occupies the ground floor of the old industrial building on Innherredsveien, windows facing Solsiden's restaurant row — one of Trondheim's most popular gym chains with 14,000 members and doors open from five in the morning.

Stovner Torg is built right around the T-bane station — 3 minutes on foot from the Grorud line and under 30 minutes to Oslo city centre on lines 4 and 5. Stovner Senter is the adjacent building with groceries, a pharmacy, a library and a wide range of services. A new swimming and fitness facility opens summer 2026 right next to the project, and surrounding it all is a forest district with local parks and trails leading to Gjelleråsmarka and Østmarka.

Overvik sits between the Trondheim Fjord and Estenstadmarka forest, on the heights above Ranheim. Close to the sea with hiking trails right outside your door, and everything you need in daily life within short distance.

Scandic Nidelven sits where the River Nid meets the fjord, in the heart of Trondheim's most vibrant district. From here, the city's best restaurants, Norway's national rock museum, and a thriving cultural scene are all within walking distance.

Tiller is Trondheim's most comprehensive district south of the city center — a hub where City Syd, TillerTorget and a wide range of restaurants, fitness centers and everyday services sit within a compact footprint. The hotel is positioned right in the middle, with most amenities within walking distance and frequent bus connections into the city center.

Nøstebukten Brygge sits on the peninsula between Vågen and Puddefjorden, where Nøstet meets the sea. The city centre is a ten-minute walk away — Bryggen, the Fish Market and Festplassen all lie along the same route. Nordnes-Nøstet is one of Bergen's most distinctive neighbourhoods, with wooden architecture, the Nordnes outdoor pool, and short distances to both culture and everyday services.

Quality Airport Hotel Værnes sits in the center of Stjørdal, with Kjøpmannsgata and Torgkvartalet as its closest neighbors. The neighborhood offers surprisingly much — from local craft bakeries and specialty cafés to cultural centers, gyms, and green city parks, all within walking distance.

Sirkus Shopping with Coop Mega, a pharmacy and a hundred stores within nine minutes on foot — Coop Prix Persaunet for quick errands. Hairdresser and groceries without getting in the car.
Louiselyst Gård in stately 1840s surroundings and Il Fornaio with stone-oven Italian pizza offer two different directions — cafes and bakeries follow with Sirkus Shopping within walking distance.

Ladestien along the fjord starts a short bike ride away — eight kilometres of coastal trail with bathing spots and sea air. Parks and green spaces within fifteen minutes on foot provide daily contact with nature.

Leangen station with regional trains to the city centre and northward, twelve bus stops within walking distance and ten city bike stations. The district is planned car-free — the infrastructure for public transport and cycling is already in place.

3T-Leangen with spinning, hot yoga and squash, Grip climbing centre with Norway's tallest indoor climbing wall, and Trondheim Performance Center three minutes away. Range and proximity in the same neighbourhood.
Valentinlyst Senter within walking distance — grocery, pharmacy and everyday services under one roof, with further options along Valentinlystveien.

Fagerborggaten barnehage (kindergarten) is just around the corner from Vibes gate — a municipal option within a five-minute walk. Bolteløkka skole, the designated primary school for the address, serves grades 1 through 7 and is five minutes away.
Everyday needs are covered in every direction from Vibes gate. Extra in Theresesgate and Extra at Bislett are both a few minutes away, and Coop Mega Bislett rounds out the options eight minutes west.

Good Bread Bisletthjørnet is the neighbourhood's artisan bakery — stone-oven baked bread, croissants and espresso, five minutes from Vibes gate. Delicatessen Majorstuen is nearby: a tapas restaurant with Spanish cuisine and a curated selection of Iberian wines.

Stensparken begins just a few minutes from the front door and serves as the neighbourhood's green backbone — a natural ridge with paths, viewpoints and mature vegetation in the heart of the city. Dronning Astrids park and Marienlystparken are both within eight minutes and offer open green spaces in quiet urban surroundings.

Deichman Majorstuen, Oslo's largest local library in the district, is eight minutes from Vibes gate — with books, digital media and study spaces across multiple floors. The Historical Museum is a fifteen-minute walk and houses collections spanning ancient antiquity to Norwegian medieval history, including one of the country's most important Viking Age collections.

Bislett stop is five minutes from Vibes gate, served by tram lines 12 and 19 — two lines connecting Bislett and Majorstuen to the city centre, Grünerløkka and Ljabru. Majorstuen T-bane station, eight minutes west, gathers all westbound metro lines and provides the fastest connection to Nationaltheatret and Stortinget.

SATS Bislett is the fitness centre in the Bislett quarter, five minutes from Vibes gate — one of the chain's larger facilities with group classes, free weights, a Reformer studio and a Hot Yoga hall. Bislet Bad & Trening next door combines historic surroundings with a complete strength and cardio gym plus a swimming pool, open for individual training and courses.
Rommen skole is a combined primary and lower secondary school for years 1–9 — pupils do not need to change school.
Stovner Senter is the adjacent building — groceries, pharmacy, library and services from 4 minutes on foot.
Around Stovner Torg the dining offer is defined by international breadth — Turkish grill, Asian fusion and Nordic café.
Stovner is a forest district — green spaces within walking distance and a short hop to Gjelleråsmarka from Vestli T-bane.
Cultural life in Stovner centres on a library, a performing arts venue and community houses within walking distance.
Stovner T-bane is a 3-minute walk from Stovner Torg — lines 4 and 5 on the Grorud line with direct services to the city centre.
Stovner bad opens summer 2026 right next to the project — a 2-minute walk from Stovner Torg.
Fjellsdalen skole, serving the Våkleivskogen area, is a 10-minute walk. For kindergarten, Våtun barnehage and Våkleivbrotet Kanvas-barnehage are just 3 and 4 minutes from the neighbourhood.

Bønes centre brings together the daily essentials — REMA 1000, SPAR, and Bunnpris are all within the local shopping area, a 6-minute walk. For pharmacy services and a wider range of shops, Oasen district centre in Fyllingsdalen is a short bus ride away.
Bønes Pizzeria is the neighbourhood's go-to for evening takeaway. Along Nordåsvannet, an 8-minute walk away, Fagernes Yacht Club offers waterside dining with views across the fjord.

Kyrkjetangen is the neighbourhood's swimming spot on Nordåsvannet — a 13-minute walk — with sandy beaches, rock ledges, a diving board, and barbecue areas. From here you can rent a canoe and paddle towards Marmorøyen.

Fyllingsdalen library is located centrally in Oasen centre and is part of the Bergen Public Library network. Bønes Arena serves as the neighbourhood's multi-use venue for community-led culture and sport.
Bønes is connected to Bergen city centre via bus routes 14 and 15, both departing from Bønes senter, a 6-minute walk. The nearest bus stop, Sælenveien nr 36, is just 3 minutes away.

Living Yoga is a 6-minute walk from the neighbourhood, offering yoga and Pilates classes. Sporty Bergen Bønes is the largest gym in the area, 9 minutes on foot, with free weights, machines, and group classes.
Byhaven shopping center is literally on the doorstep, and Trondheim Torg and Middelhavets Marked cover the rest of your daily needs within a short walk.
With Rockheim as your nearest neighbor and Cinemateket around the corner, live concerts, film screenings, and art exhibitions are never far away.
From Britannia Hotel's award-winning restaurants to Backstube's artisan bakery on Jomfrugata — the neighborhood offers everything from fine dining to everyday coffee stops.
Bus stops and city bikes right outside the hotel, with Trondheim Central Station within walking distance — you rarely need more than your feet to get around.
3T-Midtby'n is three minutes away, and the neighborhood has everything from strength training and martial arts to pilates and yoga.
Families at Overvik belong to the Ranheim Vest school district. Ranheim skole, the local primary school for grades 1–7, is about fifteen minutes on foot.
Vettre primary school serves Langenga's catchment area — grades 1–7, eight minutes' walk from the project.

The Brøset district is built for families: 53 per cent green space, reduced car access, and a new grade 1-7 school opening in summer 2026 — right as residents move in. Brøset skole replaces the current pavilion on Granåsvegen and will house 525 pupils with its own sports hall.

Five minutes on foot from Wesselsløkka lies Valentinlyst Senter — one of Norway's oldest neighbourhood centres, opened 1975. Coop Mega handles the weekly shop, Vinmonopolet sits on the corner, and Boots Apotek operates in the same building.
The dining scene around Wesselsløkka is everyday and locally grounded. VYDA Restaurant sits two minutes from the front door with Vietnamese cuisine and its own children's menu.

The Brøset district is built around green space, not beside it — 53 per cent of the area is park and near-nature. Brøset Hundepark is two minutes from Wesselsløkka and acts as the neighbourhood's informal meeting spot.

The neighbourhood has a local library and direct bus to the city's full cultural programme. Moholt bibliotek — nineteen minutes on foot or a short cycle — is open 07 to 23 every day with an access card, and includes a dedicated children's section with events.
Brøset Hageby bus stop sits 39 metres from the front door, with line 12 providing an eight-minute direct service to Trondheim city centre. The 113 night bus covers the return from town.
Five fitness centres lie within ten minutes of Wesselsløkka. Fresh Fitness Valentinlyst is closest — five minutes away, open 05 to 24 every day, free weights and group sessions at the budget end.
MENY, Byhaven and Olavskvartalet are within walking distance from Stasjonskvartalet. Pharmacy, hairdresser and grocery — everything daily life requires is under ten minutes on foot.

Nøstebukten lies in the Nordnes school district, with the primary school six minutes away and kindergartens spread along the peninsula. Sports halls, the outdoor pool and Nordnes Park all sit within the same neighbourhood.
Daily errands sit along Strandgaten and Vågsbunnen. Groceries are within a ten-minute walk from the waterfront, and pharmacies cluster around the Fish Market and Bryggen.

Nøstegaten anchors the local café and bakery scene, and the restaurant streets stretch from Strandkaien to Engen. The range spans from a French bakery to modern Nordic kitchens and Northern Europe's oldest rock club.
Nordnes Park lies at the tip of the peninsula, an eleven-minute walk from the project. Nordnes Sjøbad — the city's heated outdoor saltwater pool — sits six minutes away with direct access to the sea.
The cultural quarter begins right outside the door — USF Verftet is four minutes away, Bergen Cinema six. The ring of museums around Bryggen and Bergenhus all sit within a fifteen-minute walk.
Jektevik Terminal lies two minutes away, and central Bergen is covered by the Skyss bus network. The Bybanen light rail to Flesland and Åsane is reached at Kaigaten, an eleven-minute walk away.
Gyms and spas are split between Nøstet and Bryggen, and Laugaren — the floating sauna at USF Verftet — sits two minutes from the project.
Torgkvartalet with Coop Mega and a pharmacy is two minutes away. Kjøpmannsgata has everything from hairdressers to interior shops — everyday needs are easy to handle on foot from the hotel.

Kimen cultural center is the hub of Stjørdal's cultural life — with cinema, library, and exhibitions under one roof. Kimenparken right outside is the gathering point, and for those who want to venture further, Monsberga and Sandskogan offer forest and views.

From five-star Gjøken Kaffe & Vinbar with locally roasted coffee to family favorite G. Johnsen bakery, serving fresh bread from Kjøpmannsgata since 1900 — the food scene in Stjørdal center is more varied than you might think.
Stjørdal torg bus stop is a two-minute walk away and gives you direct connections to Trondheim and Værnes airport. The train to Trondheim takes under half an hour.
With everything from 3T and Feel24 open around the clock to calm yoga studios and Thai massage — it's easy to keep up your training routine or just relax after a long day.

The station quarter is not primarily a family enclave, but the groundwork is in place. Three playgrounds along the waterfront sit within six minutes on foot — at Brattørkaia, TMV-kaia, and beside Pirbadet.

Daily needs are handled without leaving the station neighbourhood. Byhaven and Olavskvartalet sit in the adjacent block — four to five minutes on foot — with Vitusapotek, Vinmonopolet, and everyday services under two roofs.

From the waterfront, the dining scene is two to four minutes away on foot. Troll Restaurant on Fosenkaia builds a Trøndelag-sourced kitchen around cod tongue and a menu that shifts with the sea chart.

From the front door you step straight onto the harbour promenade along Brattørkaia. It runs westward toward Munkholmen on the horizon, past Rockheim Park and Krigsseilerplassen with views across the fjord.

The station neighbourhood sits close to the city's culture. Rockheim — Norway's national museum of popular music — stands three minutes away in its recognisable silo with a golden box suspended over the fjord.

Trondheim S sits 85 metres from the front door — direct trains to Oslo, Bodø, and Östersund, with the Dovre, Nordland, Røros, and Meråker lines all starting here. The express boat terminal is two minutes on foot: Norled route 810 to Vanvikan in thirteen minutes, route 800 onward to Kristiansund via Hitra.
Along the waterfront you find Stu — floating sauna rafts designed and built by thirteen NTNU architecture students — four minutes away, with warm rooms opening directly onto the fjord year round.
City Syd and TillerTorget cover most needs — from Obs and MENY groceries to Boots apotek and Hårgalleriet, all within a short walk.
Everyday essentials are within a fifteen-minute walk from Overvik. Groceries are under ten minutes west toward Olderdalen and about fifteen minutes south toward Charlottenlund.
Trekanten at Asker station is the hub for everyday life — groceries, pharmacy and services gathered a short bus ride from Langenga.
MENY and Extra Rosenborg within walking distance, pharmacy at Solsiden, and a hairdresser just around the corner — daily errands handled without taking the car.
Tiller leans more toward everyday life than cultural landmarks, but KVT Bibliotek provides a quiet retreat amid the retail bustle, and Grusbanen is there for a quick walk outdoors.
Overvik's café and restaurant scene is taking shape — Dromedar Kaffebar has opened next to the project. Toward Ranheim centre, pizzerias and established eateries sit within a fifteen-minute walk.
Asker centre is the natural food destination — coffee bars, bakeries and restaurants clustered around Trekanten and the station.
Between Adressaparken and Rockheim, with three hotels, five museums, and the Nidelva riverside path outside the door — a neighbourhood with urban breadth and green along the river.

Overvik sits between fjord and forest — Trondheim fjord to the north, Estenstadmarka to the south. The forest trails are a short cycle away, and bathing spots along the fjord are around twenty minutes on foot.
Bondivannet begins just below the project and offers walking access to Asker's most distinctive nature reserve.

Culture and leisure venues cluster around Ranheim centre, about fifteen minutes on foot from Overvik. Kulturtribunen and Ranheim library share space in the grandstand building at Ranheim sports complex.
Asker cultural centre and Trekanten are the neighbourhood's cultural hub.
Transport options come in two tiers: bus stops in the neighbourhood and train service from Ranheim station. The nearest bus stop is five minutes on foot, Ranheim station about fifteen.
Bondivann station on the Spikkestad line is the project's nearest train station — direct line to Asker and Oslo.
Exercise and activity venues concentrate around Ranheim sports complex, about fifteen minutes on foot from Overvik. Fitness centre, sports halls and outdoor courts share the same site.
Risenga sports complex is Asker's sporting hub — ten minutes' walk from Langenga.
